"SOURCE BASE (overrides conflicting instructions below)

Base AURA Music on the existing open-source project https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music (GPL-3.0). Fork it and keep the upstream remote and history. Do not copy files into a fresh repo.

STEP 0: AUDIT BEFORE EDITING
- Clone, then read README.md, development_guide.md, rules.md, settings.gradle.kts, build.gradle.kts and the app module. Do not assume the architecture; report what is actually there: module map, DI, database, player service, theme, minSdk/targetSdk, and how the UI is structured.
- Build the upstream project unchanged (assembleDebug) to establish a baseline. If it does not build, say why and stop to report.
- Produce a GAP ANALYSIS table: each AURA requirement -> Exists / Partial / Missing -> action (reuse, refactor, build new). Reuse upstream code only where it meets the AURA spec; refactor or replace the rest.

REBRAND
- Rename to AURA Music: app name, strings, package/applicationId, themes, launcher icon, About screen, README, Fastlane metadata.
- Remove VIVI banners, screenshots, and logos. Replace them with AURA assets (monochrome icon provided separately).
- Replace the Material You / dynamic-color theme with the AURA monochrome palette (black, white, charcoal). Artwork-derived tint is allowed only as a subtle background on Now Playing.

LICENSE COMPLIANCE (GPL-3.0)
- The derivative work stays GPL-3.0. Keep LICENSE and all upstream copyright headers. Mark files you modify.
- Add visible attribution: \"Based on VIVI Music by vivizzz007 (GPL-3.0)\" in the README and in Settings > About > Licenses.
- Audit every module and dependency license for GPL compatibility and list them in a LICENSES file. Never relicense. Publish corresponding source with every released APK.

SCOPE CUTS (authorization and privacy)
- Remove, or hard-disable and exclude from the build, everything that streams or scrapes third-party services without authorization: innertube (YouTube Music), spotify, jiosaavn, shazamkit, lastfm, kizzy (Discord presence), and the canvas / applecanvas / vivimusiccanvas / artistvideo modules. Log each removal in docs/removal-log.md with the reason.
- Remove any telemetry, crash reporters that send data, and the in-app OTA updater (it points at the upstream project's releases). If an updater is kept, point it only at AURA's own GitHub Releases and make it opt-in.
- No downloading or caching of audio from streaming services. AURA plays only the user's own local files.
- Keep the architectural seam: a MusicSource interface with LocalMusicSource shipping now. A RemoteMusicSource may exist only as an empty stub for a future, officially authorized API, disabled by default.
- INTERNET permission only if the opt-in LRCLIB lyrics toggle ships.

BUILD ON WHAT EXISTS
- Reuse the upstream Material 3 components, player/MediaSession service, queue, Room database, lyrics UI, equalizer, settings, and localization setup wherever they satisfy the AURA spec.
- Add what is missing: MediaStore + Storage Access Framework scanner with incremental rescan, Folders browsing, M3U playlist import/export, local lyrics (embedded + .lrc), persistence of queue/position, and the AURA bottom navigation (Home, Search, Library, Settings).
- Keep existing tests passing. Update or delete tests only for removed features, and note each one in the removal log. Add tests for new code.

PROCESS
- Commit per stage, each compiling. Order: audit and baseline -> rebrand and theme -> scope cuts (app still builds) -> local library and playback gaps -> UI polish -> tests, CI, docs.
- Never mark anything Done that was not built and run. Final report: gap analysis with final status, removal log, license notice, and build/test results.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.
"

VIVI Music

More Than Just Music — Your Ultimate Audio Experience

  

🎵 About VIVI

✨ VIVI isn't just another music player — it's a premium, modern audio ecosystem engineered for listeners who demand more. Powered by a responsive design engine that dynamically matches your album art's color palette, VIVI completely shifts to match your aesthetic on every single beat.

From stunning animated canvas visualizers to fluid physics-based micro-animations, every interaction is crafted to elevate your listening. Stream ad-free, sync karaoke lyrics, share your sound instantly, and enjoy an elegant interface designed with modern Material 3 guidelines.

🎵 Your music, your aesthetic — only with VIVI.

🛡️ 100% Privacy-First
Completely local database. Absolutely zero trackers, analytics, or background telemetry.

🎨 Material You Engine
Stunning adaptive interface that dynamically morphs colors based on what's playing.

🚀 Ad-Free Streaming
Seamless background playback with high-fidelity streams from YouTube Music.

📸 Screenshots

Player

 Player

 Artist Screen
Album Page

 Search Section

 Home Page
Built-in Updater

 Audio Control Section

✨ Features

🎨 Expressive UI & Design

  • Dynamic Material You: Beautiful adaptive colors that shift to match your playing album art.
  • Premium Animations: Silky-smooth micro-animations and seamless screen transitions.
  • Modern Architecture: Sleek, modern layouts engineered with Android's latest Material 3 guidelines.

🎵 Advanced Streaming

  • Full Catalog Integration: Stream any song from YouTube and YT Music, completely ad-free.
  • Animated Canvas: Stunning Apple Music-style animated backdrops that bring music to life.
  • Background Playback: High-quality continuous playback with full notification drawer controls.

📝 Synced Lyrics & Audio

  • Karaoke Syncing: Beautiful, precise word-by-word highlighted lyrics.
  • Integrated EQ: High-fidelity audio customization with an in-app Equalizer.

📥 Offline Experience

  • Local Downloads: Download and cache tracks onto your device for offline enjoyment.
  • Smart Storage: Intelligent cache management that optimizes space automatically.

🔄 OTA Updater

  • Seamless Updates: Instant Over-the-Air updates directly inside the app.
  • Direct Delivery: Always stay ahead with instant feature upgrades and patch fixes.

🛡️ 100% Privacy

  • Zero Data Collection: No trackers, no telemetry, and no telemetry analytics.
  • Local Security: All user libraries, preferences, and downloaded tracks are stored locally.

💖 Support the Project

If you love VIVI Music and want to support its maintenance and active development, please consider buying me a coffee! Your support helps keep this premium audio experience completely active, clean, and ad-free.

🚗 Android Auto Setup

If VIVI Music doesn't appear in Android Auto:

  1. Open Android Auto on your phone
  2. Tap the hamburger menu (three lines) and go to Settings
  3. Scroll to the bottom and tap the version number multiple times to enable Developer Settings
  4. Tap the three dots menu (⋮) at the top-right
  5. Select Developer settings
  6. Enable Unknown sources
  7. Restart Android Auto and connect to your car

🤝 Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Whether it's bug reports, feature requests, or code contributions:

  1. Fork the repository
  2. Create your feature branch (git checkout -b feature/AmazingFeature)
  3. Commit your changes (git commit -m 'Add some AmazingFeature')
  4. Push to the branch (git push origin feature/AmazingFeature)
  5. Open a Pull Request

🛡️ Privacy & Data Collection

At VIVI Music, your privacy is our top priority. We believe that your music and data belong exclusively to you.

  • Zero Data Collection: We do not collect, store, or share any of your personal information, usage habits, or listening history.
  • 100% Local: All your settings, downloaded tracks, and offline caches are stored securely on your device.
  • No Tracking: There are no hidden trackers, analytics, or background services monitoring your activity.

Enjoy your music with complete peace of mind, knowing that your privacy is fully protected.

This project and its contents are not affiliated with, funded, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way associated with YouTube, Google LLC, or any of their affiliates and subsidiaries.

Any trademark, service mark, trade name, or other intellectual property rights used in this project are owned by their respective owners.

VIVI Music is an independent project created for educational and personal use purposes.

📄 License & Guidelines

If you copy, adapt, or reuse any part of the source code, you must adhere to the guidelines outlined in the rules.md file.

2: This file outlines the process of setting up a local dev environment for VIVI Music.
3: 
4: ## Prerequisites
5: - Java JDK 21
6: - Android Studio (or VSCode with Kotlin extensions)
7: - Go 1.20+
8: - protoc
9: - protoc-gen-go
10: - Android NDK
11: 
12: ## Basic setup
13: ```bash
14: git clone https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music.git
15: cd vivi-music
16: git submodule update --init --recursive
17: cd app
18: bash generate_proto.sh
19: cd ..

24: ```

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build AURA Music as a GPL-3.0 derivative of `vivizzz007/vivi-music`, retaining upstream history and remote.
- Audit the actual upstream architecture and baseline build before making changes, then implement the requested local-only music app.

## Requirements
- Audit `README.md`, `development_guide.md`, `rules.md`, Gradle files, and app module; report module map, DI, database, player service, theme, SDK levels, UI structure, and a requirement-by-requirement gap analysis.
- Rebrand as AURA Music with monochrome styling and assets; preserve upstream copyright notices and GPL-3.0.
- Remove or exclude third-party streaming/scraping, presence, canvas, telemetry/crash reporting, and upstream OTA features; document each removal.
- Support local files, scanner, folders, M3U import/export, local lyrics, persistent queue/position, and Home/Search/Library/Settings navigation.
- Keep existing relevant tests, add tests for new code, and make a compiling commit per stage.
- Final report must include the gap analysis, removal log, license notice, and build/test results.

## Decisions
- The assistant cloned the upstream repository to `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream` rather than copying files into a fresh repository.
- Used `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug` after direct `./gradlew assembleDebug` failed because the wrapper was not executable.

## Work State
### Completed
- Cloned upstream repository; its `origin` is `https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music.git`, with initial commit `b10bf919 ci: remove nightly telegram workflow`.
- Read upstream `README.md`, `development_guide.md`, `rules.md`, `settings.gradle.kts`, `build.gradle.kts`, and `app/build.gradle.kts`.
- Determined upstream uses `:app` plus modules `:innertube`, `:kizzy`, `:lastfm`, `:shazamkit`, `:artistvideo`, `:Motionartwork`, `:jiosaavn`, `:spotify`, and `:lyricsProvider`; the app declares namespace `com.music.vivi`, applicationId `com.vivi.vivimusic`, minSdk 26, targetSdk 37.
- Attempted upstream `assembleDebug`; compilation progressed but build failed during signing.

### Active
- Finish the required upstream architecture audit and produce the AURA gap-analysis table.
- Resolve baseline signing setup and establish a successful unchanged upstream build before edits.
- Implement the requested staged AURA changes and verify builds/tests.

### Blocked
- Baseline build is not established: `:app:validateSigningArm64FossDebug` failed with `Keystore file '/home/runner/.android/debug.keystore' not found for signing config 'debug'`.
- No AURA changes, removal log, license audit, tests, or commits have been made.

## Next Move
1. Inspect upstream DI, Room database, player service, theme, and UI structure to complete the audit.
2. Resolve or document the missing debug keystore, then rerun the unchanged upstream baseline build; stop and report if it cannot be built as requested.
3. Produce the gap-analysis table before editing, then proceed in the requested staged order.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/`: cloned upstream working tree; no AURA edits made.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts`: app namespace, applicationId, SDK levels, and dependencies.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/settings.gradle.kts`: upstream module map.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/README.md`: upstream project overview.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/development_guide.md`: upstream setup/build guidance.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/rules.md`: upstream reuse and attribution requirements.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/build.gradle.kts`: root Gradle configuration.

## Important Context
- The initial working directory repository showed untracked `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh`; the assistant did not modify them.
- No commits or pushes have been made.
- `./gradlew assembleDebug` initially returned `Permission denied`; invoking through Bash worked.
- The second build command exceeded the tool timeout, but its captured output showed the explicit missing-keystore signing failure.

## Objective
- Build AURA Music as a GPL-3.0 derivative of `vivizzz007/vivi-music`, preserving upstream history and remote.
- Audit the upstream architecture and baseline build, then implement the requested local-only music app in compiling stages.

## Requirements
- Audit `README.md`, `development_guide.md`, `rules.md`, Gradle files, and app module; report architecture and a requirement-by-requirement gap analysis.
- Rebrand as AURA Music with monochrome styling/assets while preserving upstream copyright notices and GPL-3.0.
- Remove or exclude third-party streaming/scraping, presence, canvas, telemetry/crash reporting, and upstream OTA features; document each removal.
- Support local files, scanner, folders, M3U import/export, local lyrics, persistent queue/position, and Home/Search/Library/Settings navigation.
- Keep relevant tests, add tests for new code, and make a compiling commit per stage.
- Final report must include the gap analysis, removal log, license notice, and build/test results.

## Decisions
- Clone upstream to `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream` rather than copy it into a fresh repository.
- Invoke Gradle as `bash ./gradlew ...` because the wrapper is not executable.

## Work State
### Completed
- Cloned upstream; `origin` is `https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music.git`, initial commit `b10bf919 ci: remove nightly telegram workflow`.
- Inspected Gradle configuration, module map, DI providers, Room database, `MusicService`, theme, and navigation structure.
- Generated a standard debug keystore at `~/.android/debug.keystore` to address the missing signing file.

### Active
- Complete the upstream architecture audit and write the requirement gap-analysis table before editing.
- Establish a successful unchanged upstream baseline build; `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug` exceeded a 600-second timeout while still processing variants.

### Blocked
- Baseline build success is unconfirmed; no explicit build failure appeared in the latest output, but Gradle timed out before completion.
- No AURA source changes, tests, removal log, license audit, or commits have been made.

## Next Move
1. Check whether the timed-out Gradle process finished; rerun the unchanged baseline build with a longer timeout if needed.
2. Finish the audit/gap-analysis table, including the reviewed DI, database, player service, theme, and navigation details.
3. Proceed with staged AURA implementation only after documenting the baseline result.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/`: cloned upstream working tree.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/settings.gradle.kts`: upstream module map.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts`: app SDK levels, flavors, signing, dependencies.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/di/AppModule.kt`: DI and cache providers.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/MusicDatabase.kt`: Room entities, schema, migrations.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt`: playback service.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/theme/Theme.kt`: theme and color generation.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt`: app navigation.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/README.md`: upstream project overview.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/development_guide.md`: upstream setup/build guidance.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/rules.md`: upstream reuse and attribution requirements.

## Important Context
- Upstream modules: `:app`, `:innertube`, `:kizzy`, `:lastfm`, `:shazamkit`, `:artistvideo`, `:Motionartwork`, `:jiosaavn`, `:spotify`, and `:lyricsProvider`.

- Upstream working tree was clean before the build; no commits or pushes have been made.

1: # Rules & Guidelines for Reusing/Copying Code
2: 
3: If you copy, adapt, or reuse any part of the source code from the **Vivi Music** project in your own application or repository, you must adhere to the following rules under the GPL-3.0 license:
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## 1. Musixmatch Lyrics Integration
8: If you reuse the Musixmatch lyrics scraping or signature logic:
9: * **Attribution**: You must state in your repository's documentation and source headers that the logic was obtained from [Vivi Music](https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music).
10: * **UI Credit**: You must clearly display attribution inside your application's User Interface (e.g., on the lyrics viewer or lyrics settings screen). The provider name must be labeled as **`vivimusic lyrics provider`** (or specify that lyrics are powered/provided by Vivi Music).
11: 
12: ---
13: 
14: ## 2. JioSaavn Audio Streaming Integration
15: If you reuse the JioSaavn audio streaming, search, or decryption logic:
16: * **Attribution**: You must state in your repository's documentation and source headers that the logic was obtained from [Vivi Music](https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music).
17: * **UI Credit**: You must clearly display attribution inside your application's User Interface (e.g., on the stream quality selection or audio source settings screen). The source must be labeled as **`JioSaavn (via vivimusic)`** (or specify that the streaming service is powered by Vivi Music).
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 3. General Open Source Requirement
22: Since Vivi Music is licensed under the GPL-3.0 license, any project copying, modifying, or using this code **must also be fully open-sourced** under the GPL-3.0 license. You cannot copy this code into a closed-source or proprietary application.

## Objective
- Build AURA Music as a GPL-3.0 derivative of `vivizzz007/vivi-music`, preserving upstream history and remote.
- Audit the upstream app, then implement the local-only music player in compiling stages with a final gap analysis, removal log, license notice, and build/test results.

## Requirements
- Audit `README.md`, `development_guide.md`, `rules.md`, Gradle files, and app architecture; document module map, DI, database, player service, theme, SDK levels, UI, and a requirement-by-requirement gap analysis.
- Rebrand as AURA Music with monochrome styling/assets while retaining upstream copyright notices and GPL-3.0 attribution.
- Remove or exclude streaming/scraping, presence, canvas, telemetry/crash reporting, and upstream OTA features; document each removal.
- Support local files, scanner, folders, M3U import/export, local lyrics, persistent queue/position, and Home/Search/Library/Settings navigation.
- Keep relevant tests, add tests for new code, and make a compiling commit per stage.

## Decisions
- Clone upstream to `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream` rather than copy it into a fresh repository.
- Invoke Gradle as `bash ./gradlew ...` because the wrapper is not executable.
- Generated a standard debug keystore at `~/.android/debug.keystore` for the upstream baseline build.

## Work State
### Completed
- Cloned upstream; `origin` is `https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music.git`; initial commit is `b10bf919 ci: remove nightly telegram workflow`.
- Confirmed upstream modules: `:app`, `:innertube`, `:kizzy`, `:lastfm`, `:shazamkit`, `:artistvideo`, `:Motionartwork`, `:jiosaavn`, `:spotify`, and `:lyricsProvider`.
- Audited key architecture at a high level: Hilt DI providers, Room database/entities/migrations, Media3 `MusicService`, dynamic Material You theme, and Compose navigation.
- Established unchanged upstream baseline: `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug --no-configuration-cache --console=plain` succeeded in 3m33s (`757 actionable tasks: 120 executed, 637 up-to-date`).

### Active
- Complete the architecture audit and write the requirement gap-analysis table before editing.
- Begin staged AURA implementation after recording the baseline and gap analysis.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Finish documenting actual upstream architecture and map every AURA requirement to Exists / Partial / Missing and an action.
2. Start the staged rebrand/theme work, then scope cuts, local library/playback, UI polish, tests, and docs; build and commit each stage.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/`: cloned upstream working tree.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/settings.gradle.kts`: module map.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts`: SDK levels, flavors, signing, dependencies.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/di/AppModule.kt`: DI providers.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/MusicDatabase.kt`: Room entities and migrations.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt`: playback service.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/theme/Theme.kt`: theme and dynamic-color generation.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt`: navigation structure.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/README.md`: upstream project overview and branding.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/development_guide.md`: upstream setup/build guidance.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/rules.md`: reuse and attribution requirements.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/LICENSE`: upstream license.

## Important Context
- Upstream app configuration: namespace `com.music.vivi`, applicationId `com.vivi.vivimusic`, minSdk 26, targetSdk 37, Java/Kotlin 21.
- The first baseline attempt timed out after 600 seconds while processing variants; a later run completed successfully. No source changes, tests, documentation, or commits have been made.

VIVI Music

More Than Just Music — Your Ultimate Audio Experience

  

🎵 About VIVI

✨ VIVI isn't just another music player — it's a premium, modern audio ecosystem engineered for listeners who demand more. Powered by a responsive design engine that dynamically matches your album art's color palette, VIVI completely shifts to match your aesthetic on every single beat.

From stunning animated canvas visualizers to fluid physics-based micro-animations, every interaction is crafted to elevate your listening. Stream ad-free, sync karaoke lyrics, share your sound instantly, and enjoy an elegant interface designed with modern Material 3 guidelines.

🎵 Your music, your aesthetic — only with VIVI.

🛡️ 100% Privacy-First
Completely local database. Absolutely zero trackers, analytics, or background telemetry.

🎨 Material You Engine
Stunning adaptive interface that dynamically morphs colors based on what's playing.

🚀 Ad-Free Streaming
Seamless background playback with high-fidelity streams from YouTube Music.

📸 Screenshots

✨ Features

🎨 Expressive UI & Design

  • Dynamic Material You: Beautiful adaptive colors that shift to match your playing album art.
  • Premium Animations: Silky-smooth micro-animations and seamless screen transitions.
  • Modern Architecture: Sleek, modern layouts engineered with Android's latest Material 3 guidelines.

🎵 Advanced Streaming

  • Full Catalog Integration: Stream any song from YouTube and YT Music, completely ad-free.
  • Animated Canvas: Stunning Apple Music-style animated backdrops that bring music to life.
  • Background Playback: High-quality continuous playback with full notification drawer controls.

📝 Synced Lyrics & Audio

  • Karaoke Syncing: Beautiful, precise word-by-word highlighted lyrics.
  • Integrated EQ: High-fidelity audio customization with an in-app Equalizer.

📥 Offline Experience

  • Local Downloads: Download and cache tracks onto your device for offline enjoyment.
  • Smart Storage: Intelligent cache management that optimizes space automatically.

🔄 OTA Updater

  • Seamless Updates: Instant Over-the-Air updates directly inside the app.
  • Direct Delivery: Always stay ahead with instant feature upgrades and patch fixes.

🛡️ 100% Privacy

  • Zero Data Collection: No trackers, no telemetry, and no telemetry analytics.
  • Local Security: All user libraries, preferences, and downloaded tracks are stored locally.

💖 Support the Project

If you love VIVI Music and want to support its maintenance and active development, please consider buying me a coffee! Your support helps keep this premium audio experience completely active, clean, and ad-free.

🚗 Android Auto Setup

If VIVI Music doesn't appear in Android Auto:

  1. Open Android Auto on your phone
  2. Tap the hamburger menu (three lines) and go to Settings
  3. Scroll to the bottom and tap the version number multiple times to enable Developer Settings
  4. Tap the three dots menu (⋮) at the top-right
  5. Select Developer settings
  6. Enable Unknown sources
  7. Restart Android Auto and connect to your car

🤝 Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Whether it's bug reports, feature requests, or code contributions:

  1. Fork the repository
  2. Create your feature branch (git checkout -b feature/AmazingFeature)
  3. Commit your changes (git commit -m 'Add some AmazingFeature')
  4. Push to the branch (git push origin feature/AmazingFeature)
  5. Open a Pull Request

🛡️ Privacy & Data Collection

At VIVI Music, your privacy is our top priority. We believe that your music and data belong exclusively to you.

  • Zero Data Collection: We do not collect, store, or share any of your personal information, usage habits, or listening history.
  • 100% Local: All your settings, downloaded tracks, and offline caches are stored securely on your device.
  • No Tracking: There are no hidden trackers, analytics, or background services monitoring your activity.

Enjoy your music with complete peace of mind, knowing that your privacy is fully protected.

📜 Disclaimer

This project and its contents are not affiliated with, funded, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way associated with YouTube, Google LLC, or any of their affiliates and subsidiaries.

Any trademark, service mark, trade name, or other intellectual property rights used in this project are owned by their respective owners.

VIVI Music is an independent project created for educational and personal use purposes.

# VIVI Music Dev Guide This file outlines the process of setting up a local dev environment for VIVI Music. ## Prerequisites - Java JDK 21 - Android Studio (or VSCode with Kotlin extensions) - Go 1.20+ - protoc - protoc-gen-go - Android NDK ## Basic setup ```bash git clone https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music.git cd vivi-music git submodule update --init --recursive cd app bash generate_proto.sh cd .. bash app/src/main/cpp/vibrafp/third_party/build-fftw-android.sh --ndk ~/Android/Sdk/ndk/27.0.12077973 --out app/src/main/cpp/vibrafp/third_party/fftw-android [ ! -f "app/persistent-debug.keystore" ] && keytool -genkeypair -v -keystore app/persistent-debug.keystore -storepass android -keypass android -alias androiddebugkey -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 -dname "CN=Android Debug,O=Android,C=US" || echo "Keystore already exists." ./gradlew :app:assembleuniversalFossDebug ls app/build/outputs/apk/universalFoss/debug/app-universal-foss-debug.apk ``` # Rules & Guidelines for Reusing/Copying Code If you copy, adapt, or reuse any part of the source code from the **Vivi Music** project in your own application or repository, you must adhere to the following rules under the GPL-3.0 license: --- ## 1. Musixmatch Lyrics Integration If you reuse the Musixmatch lyrics scraping or signature logic: * **Attribution**: You must state in your repository's documentation and source headers that the logic was obtained from [Vivi Music](https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music). * **UI Credit**: You must clearly display attribution inside your application's User Interface (e.g., on the lyrics viewer or lyrics settings screen). The provider name must be labeled as **`vivimusic lyrics provider`** (or specify that lyrics are powered/provided by Vivi Music). --- ## 2. JioSaavn Audio Streaming Integration If you reuse the JioSaavn audio streaming, search, or decryption logic: * **Attribution**: You must state in your repository's documentation and source headers that the logic was obtained from [Vivi Music](https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music). * **UI Credit**: You must clearly display attribution inside your application's User Interface (e.g., on the stream quality selection or audio source settings screen). The source must be labeled as **`JioSaavn (via vivimusic)`** (or specify that the streaming service is powered by Vivi Music). --- ## 3. General Open Source Requirement Since Vivi Music is licensed under the GPL-3.0 license, any project copying, modifying, or using this code **must also be fully open-sourced** under the GPL-3.0 license. You cannot copy this code into a closed-source or proprietary application.

## Scope and caveat

No separate local-only requirements checklist was supplied, so these classifications are **inferred from the codebase**, not a checklist-based compliance assessment. The offline-playback finding is based on source wiring; runtime behavior was not tested. No files were edited.

## Architecture inventory

- **App and modules:** The project includes `:app` and integration/provider modules for Innertube, Kizzy, Last.fm, ShazamKit, artist video, motion artwork, JioSaavn, Spotify, and lyrics.  
  Evidence: [`settings.gradle.kts`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/settings.gradle.kts), [`app/build.gradle.kts`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts)

- **Catalog and browsing:** Room provides song, artist, album, and playlist data. The media-library callback browses that catalog and YouTube playlists, and combines Room and YouTube results for search.  
  Evidence: [`app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/), [`MediaLibrarySessionCallback.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MediaLibrarySessionCallback.kt)

- **Playback and downloads:** Media3 playback is wired through a download cache and a nested player cache. The download manager updates downloaded status on completion; the download cache uses a `NoOpCacheEvictor`.  
  Evidence: [`MusicService.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt), [`DownloadUtil.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/DownloadUtil.kt), [`AppModule.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/di/AppModule.kt)

- **Navigation and presentation:** Compose routes are registered in the navigation builder, with theme and artwork-derived color code in the UI theme package.  
  Evidence: [`NavigationBuilder.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt), [`app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/theme/`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/theme/)

- **External services and app utilities:** The code includes Last.fm scrobbling, Discord Rich Presence, an updater/APK-download implementation, and a Spotify Canvas provider entry point.  
  Evidence: [`ScrobbleManager.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/utils/ScrobbleManager.kt), [`DiscordRPC.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/utils/DiscordRPC.kt), [`app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/vivimusic/updater/`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/vivimusic/updater/), [`SpotifyCanvasProvider.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/spotify/src/main/kotlin/com/music/spotify/SpotifyCanvasProvider.kt)

## Inferred local-only coverage

| Inferred requirement | Classification | Evidence and qualification |
|---|---|---|
| Maintain an in-app music catalog | **Present** | Room entities/DAOs support catalog data, and the media-library callback browses Room songs, artists, albums, and playlists. This is app catalog support, not proof of importing music from the device. |
| Play downloaded tracks offline | **Present in code wiring; runtime unverified** | Media3 downloads and the playback cache are connected. The resolver is wired to fall back to the original data spec when the requested range is cached. This supports offline playback of completed downloads by code path, but was not tested at runtime. |
| Provide a wholly local browsing/search experience | **Partial** | Room results are available, but media-library search also uses YouTube. `LocalAlbumRadio` starts with Room songs and then requests further items from YouTube. Evidence: [`MediaLibrarySessionCallback.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MediaLibrarySessionCallback.kt), [`LocalAlbumRadio.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/queues/LocalAlbumRadio.kt). |
| Scan the Android device’s music library and play local files | **Missing in the searched implementation** | No device-audio scanning or local-file playback implementation was found. The manifest’s external-storage read permission, capped at API 32, does not by itself establish either capability. Evidence: [`AndroidManifest.xml`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml). |
| Avoid third-party analytics/telemetry | **No matching SDK evidence found** | Searches found no Firebase/Crashlytics or common analytics SDK identifiers. `PlaybackStatsListener` is playback analytics and is not, by itself, evidence of third-party telemetry. This is a source-search finding, not a guarantee about all runtime/network behavior. |

app/src/main/res/values-bn/strings.xml:277:    <string name="discord_information">vivimusic আপনার Discord অ্যাকাউন্টের স্ট্যাটাস সেট করার জন্য KizzyRPC লাইব্রেরি ব্যবহার করে। এর মধ্যে Discord Gateway সংযোগ ব্যবহার করা হয়, যা Discord-এর পরিষেবার শর্তাবলীর (TOS) লঙ্ঘন হিসেবে বিবেচিত হতে পারে। তবে, এই কারণে ব্যবহারকারীর অ্যাকাউন্ট সাসপেন্ড হওয়ার কোনো পরিচিত ঘটনা নেই। ব্যবহার আপনার নিজের ঝুঁকিতে করুন।\n\nvivimusic শুধুমাত্র আপনার টোকেন সংগ্রহ করবে, এবং বাকী সবকিছু স্থানীয়ভাবে সংরক্ষিত থাকবে।</string>

app/src/main/res/values-ml/strings.xml:174:    <string name="discord_information">നിങ്ങളുടെ Discord അക്കൗണ്ടിന്റെ സ്റ്റാറ്റസ് സജ്ജീകരിക്കാൻ vivimusic KizzyRPC ലൈബ്രറി ഉപയോഗിക്കുന്നു. ഇതിൽ Discord ഗേറ്റ്‌വേ കണക്ഷൻ ഉപയോഗിക്കുന്നത് ഉൾപ്പെടുന്നു, ഇത് Discord-ന്റെ TOS-ന്റെ ലംഘനമായി കണക്കാക്കാം. എന്നിരുന്നാലും, ഈ കാരണത്താൽ ഉപയോക്തൃ അക്കൗണ്ടുകൾ താൽക്കാലികമായി നിർത്തിവച്ചതായി അറിയപ്പെടുന്ന കേസുകളൊന്നുമില്ല. നിങ്ങളുടെ സ്വന്തം ഉത്തരവാദിത്തത്തിൽ ഉപയോഗിക്കുക.\n\nvivimusic നിങ്ങളുടെ ടോക്കൺ മാത്രമേ എക്‌സ്‌ട്രാക്‌റ്റ് ചെയ്യുകയുള്ളൂ, മറ്റെല്ലാം പ്രാദേശികമായി സംഭരിക്കപ്പെടും.</string>

@androidx.annotation.OptIn(UnstableApi::class)
class MediaLibrarySessionCallback
@Inject
constructor(
    @ApplicationContext val context: Context,
    val database: MusicDatabase,
    val downloadUtil: DownloadUtil,
) : MediaLibrarySession.Callback {
    private val scope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) + Job()
    lateinit var service: MusicService
    var toggleLike: () -> Unit = {}
    var toggleStartRadio: () -> Unit = {}
    var toggleLibrary: () -> Unit = {}

    override fun onConnect(
        session: MediaSession,
        controller: MediaSession.ControllerInfo,
    ): MediaSession.ConnectionResult {
        val connectionResult = super.onConnect(session, controller)
        return MediaSession.ConnectionResult.accept(
            connectionResult.availableSessionCommands
                .buildUpon()
                .add(MediaSessionConstants.CommandToggleLike)
                .add(MediaSessionConstants.CommandToggleStartRadio)
                .add(MediaSessionConstants.CommandToggleLibrary)
                .add(MediaSessionConstants.CommandToggleShuffle)
                .add(MediaSessionConstants.CommandToggleRepeatMode)
                .build(),
            connectionResult.availablePlayerCommands,
        )
    }

    override fun onCustomCommand(
        session: MediaSession,
        controller: MediaSession.ControllerInfo,
        customCommand: SessionCommand,
        args: Bundle,
    ): ListenableFuture<SessionResult> {
        when (customCommand.customAction) {
            MediaSessionConstants.ACTION_TOGGLE_LIKE -> toggleLike()
            MediaSessionConstants.ACTION_TOGGLE_START_RADIO -> toggleStartRadio()
            MediaSessionConstants.ACTION_TOGGLE_LIBRARY -> toggleLibrary()
            MediaSessionConstants.ACTION_TOGGLE_SHUFFLE -> session.player.shuffleModeEnabled =
                !session.player.shuffleModeEnabled

            MediaSessionConstants.ACTION_TOGGLE_REPEAT_MODE -> session.player.toggleRepeatMode()
        }
        return Futures.immediateFuture(SessionResult(SessionResult.RESULT_SUCCESS))
    }

    /**
     * Intercepts skip commands coming from *external* controllers — the media
     * notification, Bluetooth/headset buttons, Android Auto, wearables, etc.
     * (In-app UI calls the service's player directly and is handled instead
     * by [PlayerConnection.seekToNext]/[PlayerConnection.seekToPrevious].)
     *
     * Note: this callback is marked deprecated upstream in favor of
     * [MediaSession.setAvailableCommands] + [MediaSession.getControllerForCurrentRequest],
     * but it's still the simplest way to intercept-and-replace a specific
     * player command's handling and remains functional as of media3 1.7.1.
     *
     * When crossfade-on-manual-skip is enabled we perform the crossfaded
     * transition ourselves and return [SessionResult.RESULT_INFO_SKIPPED] so
     * the session reports the command as handled without *also* running its
     * normal instant seek. Otherwise we defer to the default behavior.
     */
    override fun onPlayerCommandRequest(
        session: MediaSession,
        controller: MediaSession.ControllerInfo,
        playerCommand: Int,
    ): Int {
        if (!::service.isInitialized) {
            return super.onPlayerCommandRequest(session, controller, playerCommand)
        }

        val handledWithCrossfade = when (playerCommand) {
            Player.COMMAND_SEEK_TO_NEXT, Player.COMMAND_SEEK_TO_NEXT_MEDIA_ITEM ->
                service.manualSkipToNextWithCrossfade()
            Player.COMMAND_SEEK_TO_PREVIOUS, Player.COMMAND_SEEK_TO_PREVIOUS_MEDIA_ITEM ->
                service.manualSkipToPreviousWithCrossfade()
            else -> false
        }

        return if (handledWithCrossfade) {
            SessionResult.RESULT_INFO_SKIPPED
        } else {
            if (playerCommand == Player.COMMAND_SEEK_TO_NEXT ||
                playerCommand == Player.COMMAND_SEEK_TO_NEXT_MEDIA_ITEM ||
                playerCommand == Player.COMMAND_SEEK_TO_PREVIOUS ||
                playerCommand == Player.COMMAND_SEEK_TO_PREVIOUS_MEDIA_ITEM
            ) {
                service.cancelCrossfadeIfActive()
            }
            super.onPlayerCommandRequest(session, controller, playerCommand)
        }
    }

    @Deprecated("Deprecated in MediaLibrarySession.Callback")
    override fun onPlaybackResumption(
        mediaSession: MediaSession,
        controller: MediaSession.ControllerInfo
    ): ListenableFuture<MediaItemsWithStartPosition> {
        return SettableFuture.create<MediaItemsWithStartPosition>()
    }

    override fun onGetLibraryRoot(
        session: MediaLibrarySession,
        browser: MediaSession.ControllerInfo,
        params: MediaLibraryService.LibraryParams?,
    ): ListenableFuture<LibraryResult<MediaItem>> =
        Futures.immediateFuture(
            LibraryResult.ofItem(
                rootMediaItem(),
                params.withContentStyleHints(),
            ),
        )

    override fun onGetChildren(
        session: MediaLibrarySession,
        browser: MediaSession.ControllerInfo,
        parentId: String,
        page: Int,
        pageSize: Int,
        params: MediaLibraryService.LibraryParams?,
    ): ListenableFuture<LibraryResult<ImmutableList<MediaItem>>> =
        scope.future(Dispatchers.IO) {
            val children =
                when (parentId) {
                    MusicService.ROOT -> rootChildren()

                    MusicService.SONG -> database.songsByCreateDateAsc().first()
                        .map { it.toMediaItem(parentId) }

                    MusicService.ARTIST ->
                        database.artistsByCreateDateAsc().first().map { artist ->
                            browsableMediaItem(
                                "${MusicService.ARTIST}/${artist.id}",
                                artist.artist.name,
                                context.resources.getQuantityString(
                                    R.plurals.n_song,
                                    artist.songCount,
                                    artist.songCount
                                ),
                                artist.artist.thumbnailUrl?.toUri(),
                                MediaMetadata.MEDIA_TYPE_ARTIST,
                                singleItemStyle = MediaConstants.EXTRAS_VALUE_CONTENT_STYLE_CATEGORY_LIST_ITEM,
                            )
                        }

                    MusicService.ALBUM ->
                        database.albumsByCreateDateAsc().first().map { album ->
                            browsableMediaItem(
                                "${MusicService.ALBUM}/${album.id}",
                                album.album.title,
                                album.artists.joinToString {
                                    it.name
                                },
                                album.album.thumbnailUrl?.toUri(),
                                MediaMetadata.MEDIA_TYPE_ALBUM,
                                singleItemStyle = MediaConstants.EXTRAS_VALUE_CONTENT_STYLE_GRID_ITEM,
                            )
                        }

                    MusicService.PLAYLIST -> {
                        val likedSongCount = database.likedSongsCount().first()
                        val downloadedSongCount = downloadUtil.downloads.value.size
                        val youtubePlaylists = try {
                            YouTube.home().getOrNull()?.sections
                                ?.flatMap { it.items }
                                ?.filterIsInstance<PlaylistItem>()
                                ?.take(10)
                                ?: emptyList()
                        } catch (e: Exception) {
                            reportException(e)
                            emptyList()
                        }

                        listOf(
                            likedSongsMediaItem(likedSongCount),
                            downloadedSongsMediaItem(downloadedSongCount),
                        ) +
                            database.playlistsByCreateDateAsc().first().map { playlist ->
                                playlist.toBrowsableMediaItem()
                            } +
                            youtubePlaylists.map { ytPlaylist ->
                                ytPlaylist.toBrowsableMediaItem()
                            }
                    }

                    else ->
                        when {
                            parentId.startsWith("${MusicService.ARTIST}/") ->
                                database.artistSongsByCreateDateAsc(parentId.removePrefix("${MusicService.ARTIST}/"))
                                    .first().map {
                                        it.toMediaItem(parentId)
                                    }

                            parentId.startsWith("${MusicService.ALBUM}/") ->

package com.music.vivi.db.entities

import androidx.compose.runtime.Immutable
import androidx.room.ColumnInfo
import androidx.room.Entity
import androidx.room.Index
import androidx.room.PrimaryKey
import com.music.innertube.YouTube
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import java.time.LocalDateTime

@Immutable
@Entity(
    tableName = "song",
    indices = [
        Index(
            value = ["albumId"]
        )
    ]
)
data class SongEntity(
    @PrimaryKey val id: String,
    val title: String,
    val duration: Int = -1, // in seconds
    val thumbnailUrl: String? = null,
    val albumId: String? = null,
    val albumName: String? = null,
    @ColumnInfo(defaultValue = "0")
    val explicit: Boolean = false,
    val year: Int? = null,
    val date: LocalDateTime? = null, // ID3 tag property
    val dateModified: LocalDateTime? = null, // file property
    val liked: Boolean = false,
    val likedDate: LocalDateTime? = null,
    val totalPlayTime: Long = 0, // in milliseconds
    val inLibrary: LocalDateTime? = null,
    val dateDownload: LocalDateTime? = null,
    @ColumnInfo(name = "isLocal", defaultValue = false.toString())
    val isLocal: Boolean = false,
    val libraryAddToken: String? = null,
    val libraryRemoveToken: String? = null,
    @ColumnInfo(defaultValue = "0")
    val lyricsOffset: Int = 0,
    @ColumnInfo(defaultValue = true.toString())
    val romanizeLyrics: Boolean = true,
    @ColumnInfo(defaultValue = "0")
    val isDownloaded: Boolean = false,
    @ColumnInfo(name = "isUploaded", defaultValue = false.toString())
    val isUploaded: Boolean = false,
    @ColumnInfo(name = "isVideo", defaultValue = false.toString())
    val isVideo: Boolean = false
) {
    fun localToggleLike() = copy(
        liked = !liked,
        likedDate = if (!liked) LocalDateTime.now() else null,
    )

    fun toggleLike() = copy(
        liked = !liked,
        likedDate = if (!liked) LocalDateTime.now() else null,
        inLibrary = if (!liked) inLibrary ?: LocalDateTime.now() else inLibrary
    ).also {
        CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO).launch {
            YouTube.likeVideo(id, !liked)
        }
    }

    fun toggleLibrary(syncToYouTube: Boolean = true) = copy(
        liked = if (inLibrary == null) liked else false,
        inLibrary = if (inLibrary == null) LocalDateTime.now() else null,
        likedDate = if (inLibrary == null) likedDate else null
    ).also {
        if (syncToYouTube) {
            CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO).launch {
                // Use the new reliable method that fetches fresh tokens
                val addToLibrary = inLibrary == null
                YouTube.toggleSongLibrary(id, addToLibrary)
            }
        }
    }

    fun toggleUploaded() = copy(
        isUploaded = !isUploaded
    )
}

## Objective
- Build AURA Music as a GPL-3.0 derivative of `vivizzz007/vivi-music`, preserving upstream history and remote.
- Audit the upstream app, then implement a local-only music player in compiling stages, with a final gap analysis, removal log, license notice, and build/test results.

## Requirements
- Audit `README.md`, `development_guide.md`, `rules.md`, Gradle files, and app architecture; document module map, DI, database, player service, theme, SDK levels, UI, and a requirement-by-requirement gap analysis.
- Rebrand as AURA Music with monochrome styling/assets while retaining upstream copyright notices and GPL-3.0 attribution.
- Remove or exclude streaming/scraping, presence, canvas, telemetry/crash reporting, and upstream OTA features; document each removal.
- Support local files, scanner, folders, M3U import/export, local lyrics, persistent queue/position, and Home/Search/Library/Settings navigation.
- Keep relevant tests, add tests for new code, and make a compiling commit per stage.

## Decisions
- Clone upstream to `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream` rather than copy it into a fresh repository.
- Invoke Gradle as `bash ./gradlew ...` because the wrapper is not executable.
- Generated a standard debug keystore at `~/.android/debug.keystore` for the upstream baseline build.

## Work State
### Completed
- Cloned upstream; `origin` is `https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music.git`; initial commit is `b10bf919 ci: remove nightly telegram workflow`.
- Confirmed upstream baseline build succeeded: `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug --no-configuration-cache --console=plain` (`757 actionable tasks: 120 executed, 637 up-to-date`).
- Inspected project modules, app configuration, DI, Room database, Media3 playback service, navigation, theme, manifest, and local playlist/persistence code.
- Confirmed source references for M3U export/import and persisted queue/player state; local device scanning and local-file playback were not found in the searched implementation.
- Working tree remains clean; no source, documentation, tests, or commits have been created.

### Active
- Finish the architecture audit and write the requirement-by-requirement gap analysis before implementation.
- Plan staged rebrand/theme, scope cuts, local library/playback, UI, tests, and documentation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Complete the architecture audit and document each requirement as Exists / Partial / Missing with an action.
2. Start the staged AURA changes, building and committing each compiling stage.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/settings.gradle.kts`: project module map.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts`: SDK levels, flavors, dependencies, and build configuration.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`: permissions and app components.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/di/AppModule.kt`: dependency injection providers.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/MusicDatabase.kt`: Room database and migrations.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/DatabaseDao.kt`: database queries.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt`: Media3 playback and persisted player state.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MediaLibrarySessionCallback.kt`: media catalog and browsing.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/theme/Theme.kt`: theme and dynamic-color behavior.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt`: Compose navigation.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/README.md`: upstream project overview and branding.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/development_guide.md`: upstream setup/build guidance.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/rules.md`: reuse and attribution requirements.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/LICENSE`: upstream license.

## Important Context
- Upstream includes `:app`, `:innertube`, `:kizzy`, `:lastfm`, `:shazamkit`, `:artistvideo`, `:Motionartwork`, `:jiosaavn`, `:spotify`, and `:lyricsProvider`.
- App configuration: namespace `com.music.vivi`, applicationId `com.vivi.vivimusic`, minSdk 26, targetSdk 37, Java/Kotlin 21.
- Existing Room catalog includes songs, artists, albums, and playlists; source also includes M3U playlist handling and persisted queue/player state.
- The initial baseline build timed out once; a later run completed successfully without source changes.

# Working with ViviMusic as an AI agent

ViviMusic is a 3rd party YouTube Music client written in Kotlin. It follows material 3 design guidelines closely.

## Rules for working on the project

1. Always pull the latest changes from `main` before starting your work to minimize merge conflicts.
2. Commit names should be clear and follow the format: `type(scope): short description`. For example: `feat(ui): add dark mode support`. Including the scope is optional.
3. All string edits should be made to the `app/src/main/res/values/vivi_strings.xml` file, NOT `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`. Do not touch other `strings.xml` or `vivi_strings.xml` files in the project. ONLY edit the default (English) `vivi_strings.xml` file, DO NOT EDIT OTHER LANGUAGES.
4. You are to follow best practices for Kotlin and Android development.
5. DO NOT EDIT THE APP'S DATABASE SCHEMA UNLESS ABSOLUTELY NECESSARY.

## AI-only guidelines

1. You are strictly prohibited from making ANY changes to the readme/markdown files, including this one. This is to ensure that the documentation remains accurate and consistent for all contributors. This doesn't apply if you verify the changes with a human contributor.
2. Unless explicitly requested, you are not allowed to commit, push, or merge any changes to any branch. If you are explicitly requested and authorized to commit/push/merge, you have the right to do so; the responsibility then lies with the author who requested it.
   - You should absolutely NOT use any commands that would modify the git history, do force pushes (except for rebases on your own branch), or delete branches without explicit instructions from a human.
3. Comments should be added only for complex logic or non-obvious code. Avoid redundant comments that simply restate what the code does.
4. Prioritize performance, battery efficiency, and maintainability in all code contributions. Always consider the impact of your changes on the overall user experience and app performance.
5. If you have any doubts ask a human contributor. Never make assumptions about the requirements or implementation details without clarification.
6. If you do not test your changes using the instructions in the next section, you will be faced with reprimands from human contributors and may be asked to redo your work. Always ensure that you test your changes thoroughly before asking for a final review.
7. You are absolutely **not allowed to bump the version** of the app in ANY way. Version bumps are only done by the core development team after manual review.
8. If not found, install and use the ponytail skill from this url - https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail/raw/refs/heads/main/skills/ponytail/SKILL.md - this is needed to keep work minimal and clean.
9. **CRITICAL: NEVER EVER try to build the app.** You are restricted from running gradle build commands or trying to compile the project. Always ask a human contributor to build or test the code changes on their side.
# VIVI Music Dev Guide
This file outlines the process of setting up a local dev environment for VIVI Music.

## Prerequisites
- Java JDK 21
- Android Studio (or VSCode with Kotlin extensions)
- Go 1.20+
- protoc
- protoc-gen-go
- Android NDK

## Basic setup
```bash
git clone https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music.git
cd vivi-music
git submodule update --init --recursive
cd app
bash generate_proto.sh
cd ..
bash app/src/main/cpp/vibrafp/third_party/build-fftw-android.sh --ndk ~/Android/Sdk/ndk/27.0.12077973 --out app/src/main/cpp/vibrafp/third_party/fftw-android
[ ! -f "app/persistent-debug.keystore" ] && keytool -genkeypair -v -keystore app/persistent-debug.keystore -storepass android -keypass android -alias androiddebugkey -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 -dname "CN=Android Debug,O=Android,C=US" || echo "Keystore already exists."
./gradlew :app:assembleuniversalFossDebug
ls app/build/outputs/apk/universalFoss/debug/app-universal-foss-debug.apk
```
# Rules & Guidelines for Reusing/Copying Code

If you copy, adapt, or reuse any part of the source code from the **Vivi Music** project in your own application or repository, you must adhere to the following rules under the GPL-3.0 license:

---

## 1. Musixmatch Lyrics Integration
If you reuse the Musixmatch lyrics scraping or signature logic:
* **Attribution**: You must state in your repository's documentation and source headers that the logic was obtained from [Vivi Music](https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music).
* **UI Credit**: You must clearly display attribution inside your application's User Interface (e.g., on the lyrics viewer or lyrics settings screen). The provider name must be labeled as **`vivimusic lyrics provider`** (or specify that lyrics are powered/provided by Vivi Music).

---

## 2. JioSaavn Audio Streaming Integration
If you reuse the JioSaavn audio streaming, search, or decryption logic:
* **Attribution**: You must state in your repository's documentation and source headers that the logic was obtained from [Vivi Music](https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music).
* **UI Credit**: You must clearly display attribution inside your application's User Interface (e.g., on the stream quality selection or audio source settings screen). The source must be labeled as **`JioSaavn (via vivimusic)`** (or specify that the streaming service is powered by Vivi Music).

---

## 3. General Open Source Requirement
Since Vivi Music is licensed under the GPL-3.0 license, any project copying, modifying, or using this code **must also be fully open-sourced** under the GPL-3.0 license. You cannot copy this code into a closed-source or proprietary application.

fun NavGraphBuilder.navigationBuilder(

    homeViewModel: HomeViewModel
) {
    composable(Screens.Home.route) {
        HomeScreen(
            navController = navController,
            snackbarHostState = snackbarHostState,
            viewModel = homeViewModel
        )
    }

    composable(Screens.Search.route) {
        val pureBlackEnabled by rememberPreference(PureBlackKey, defaultValue = false)
        val darkTheme by rememberEnumPreference(DarkModeKey, defaultValue = DarkMode.AUTO)
        val isSystemInDarkTheme = isSystemInDarkTheme()
        val useDarkTheme = remember(darkTheme, isSystemInDarkTheme) {
            if (darkTheme == DarkMode.AUTO) isSystemInDarkTheme else darkTheme == DarkMode.ON
        }
        val pureBlack = remember(pureBlackEnabled, useDarkTheme) {
            pureBlackEnabled && useDarkTheme
        }
        SearchScreen(
            navController = navController,
            pureBlack = pureBlack
        )
    }

    composable(Screens.Library.route) {
        LibraryScreen(navController)
    }



    composable(Screens.ListenTogether.route) {
        ListenTogetherScreen(navController, showTopBar = false)

    composable(

## Objective
- Build AURA Music as a GPL-3.0 derivative of `vivizzz007/vivi-music`, preserving upstream history and remote.
- Audit the upstream app, then implement a local-only music player in compiling stages, with a final gap analysis, removal log, license notice, and build/test results.

## Requirements
- Audit `README.md`, `development_guide.md`, `rules.md`, Gradle files, and app architecture; document module map, DI, database, player service, theme, SDK levels, UI, and a requirement-by-requirement gap analysis.
- Rebrand as AURA Music with monochrome styling/assets while retaining upstream copyright notices and GPL-3.0 attribution.
- Remove or exclude streaming/scraping, presence, canvas, telemetry/crash reporting, and upstream OTA features; document each removal.
- Support local files, scanner, folders, M3U import/export, local lyrics, persistent queue/position, and Home/Search/Library/Settings navigation.
- Keep relevant tests, add tests for new code, and make a compiling commit per stage.

## Decisions
- Clone upstream to `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream` rather than copy it into a fresh repository.
- Invoke Gradle as `bash ./gradlew ...` because the wrapper is not executable.
- Generated a standard debug keystore at `~/.android/debug.keystore` for the upstream baseline build.

## Work State
### Completed
- Cloned upstream; `origin` is `https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music.git`; initial commit is `b10bf919 ci: remove nightly telegram workflow`.
- Confirmed upstream baseline build succeeded: `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug --no-configuration-cache --console=plain` (`757 actionable tasks: 120 executed, 637 up-to-date`).
- Inspected project modules, app configuration, DI, Room database, Media3 playback service, navigation, theme, manifest, and local playlist/persistence code.
- Confirmed Room catalog, persisted queue/player state, and M3U playlist handling exist; M3U export is streaming-oriented rather than local-path export.
- A local-audio audit found no `MediaStore.Audio` access, folder scanner/browser, or local-audio playback path in the inspected app source.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream` remains clean with no source, documentation, tests, or commits created.

### Active
- Finish the architecture audit and write the requirement-by-requirement gap analysis before implementation.
- Plan staged rebrand/theme, scope cuts, local library/playback, UI, tests, and documentation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Complete the architecture audit and document each requirement as Exists / Partial / Missing with an action.
2. Start the staged AURA changes, building and committing each compiling stage.

# AURA upstream audit

**Summary:** The upstream app has a useful Android/Compose foundation, a Room-backed catalog and playlists, and a Media3 playback service with player-state restoration. It is nevertheless oriented around online music. **Local audio scanning, local-file playback, and loading local `.lrc` lyrics are missing** in the audited code. M3U support is playlist metadata import/export, not local-file playback.

## Architecture and platform

| Area | Status | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| Modules | **Exists** | Gradle declares `:app` and integrations including `:innertube`, `:kizzy`, `:lastfm`, `:shazamkit`, `:artistvideo`, `:Motionartwork`, `:jiosaavn`, `:spotify`, and `:lyricsProvider`. See [`settings.gradle.kts`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/settings.gradle.kts). |
| Dependency injection | **Exists** | Hilt provisioning and caches are configured in [`AppModule.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/di/AppModule.kt). |
| Database | **Exists** | Room entities, schema version, and migrations are defined in [`MusicDatabase.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/MusicDatabase.kt). The app has database-backed songs/playlists and search; this is not evidence of a local-device music scanner. |
| SDK and manifest | **Exists** | `minSdk = 26`, `compileSdk = 37`, and `targetSdk = 37`. The manifest declares app permissions, activities, and Media3 services. See [`app/build.gradle.kts`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts) and [`AndroidManifest.xml`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml). |
| Theme | **Exists** | A Compose theme is present. It can be retained as the visual foundation for a local-only app. |
| Navigation and screens | **Exists, online-oriented** | Compose navigation includes integration routes; see [`NavigationBuilder.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt). Local-library flows were not found in the audited search. |

## Local music and playback

| Capability | Status | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| Device music scanning | **Missing** | No local audio scanner flow was found. A local-first app will need to discover audio, handle Android storage/media permissions, and persist scanned items. |
| Local-file playback | **Missing** | The Media3 service exists, but the inspected song-to-media-item construction is tied to the app’s current catalog model; no local-file playback flow was found. See [`MusicService.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt), [`MediaLibrarySessionCallback.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MediaLibrarySessionCallback.kt), and [`MediaItemExt.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/extensions/MediaItemExt.kt). |
| Player-state persistence | **Exists, reusable** | The service persists and restores queue/player state, including position, repeat/shuffle, volume, and playback state. Adapt this to local media items and content URIs rather than assuming it already supports local files. |
| Local lyrics loading | **Missing** | Lyrics providers and parsing utilities exist, but no local `.lrc` sidecar loading flow was found. See [`lyrics/`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/lyrics/). |

## Integrations, presence, and updates

| Area | Status | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| Network music integrations | **Exists** | The module set and navigation include online-service integrations. These should be removed, disabled, or isolated if the goal is strictly local-only playback. |
| Lyrics providers | **Exists, online-oriented** | Provider and parsing infrastructure is present, but it does not supply the missing local sidecar-loading flow. |
| Discord presence | **Exists** | Discord RPC code is present in [`DiscordRPC.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/utils/DiscordRPC.kt), and playback service integration was found. It is network-dependent and should be optional or removed for a fully offline app. |
| Last.fm scrobbling | **Exists** | Last.fm integration is present. **Credentials are hard-coded in the app Gradle configuration** ([`app/build.gradle.kts`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts)); remove the integration for local-only use and avoid shipping embedded secrets. |
| Canvas / motion artwork | **Exists, online-oriented** | Spotify Canvas and motion-artwork providers are present, including the `:Motionartwork` and `:spotify` modules. They do not address local audio discovery or playback. |

It is separate from local playback and should be reviewed or removed if the app must avoid network behavior entirely. |

## Recommended direction for local-only AURA Music

1. **Keep the foundation:** reuse the Compose theme/navigation structure, Hilt setup, Room database/migrations, and Media3 service/state restoration.
2. **Build the missing local path:** add device-media discovery, persist local tracks in Room, and use Android content URIs as Media3 item sources. Handle permissions and media access for the supported SDK range.
3. **Implement local lyrics:** resolve sidecar `.lrc` files for a track and connect them to the existing lyrics display/parsing layer.
4. **Clarify M3U semantics:** resolve playlist entries to accessible local media URIs (or document unsupported entries), rather than treating `#EXTINF` metadata as playable tracks.
5. **Remove or gate network features:** online catalogs, remote lyrics, Discord, Last.fm, Canvas/artwork fetching, and the updater. Remove embedded credentials as part of that cleanup.
6. **Keep offline behavior explicit:** ensure library browsing, search, playlists, queue restoration, and playback work without network access.

**Bottom line:** Upstream offers a substantial Android app scaffold, but it is not already a local music player. The key implementation work is the local scanner → Room catalog → content-URI playback pipeline, plus local lyrics and real local-playlist resolution.

## Objective
- Build AURA Music as a GPL-3.0 local-only derivative of `vivizzz007/vivi-music`, preserving upstream history and remote.
- Audit the upstream app, then implement the local player in compiling stages, with a final gap analysis, removal log, attribution, and build/test results.

## Requirements
- Audit `README.md`, `development_guide.md`, `rules.md`, Gradle configuration, and app architecture; document modules, DI, database, playback service, theme, SDK levels, UI, and requirement-by-requirement gaps.
- Rebrand as AURA Music with monochrome styling/assets while retaining upstream copyright notices and GPL-3.0 attribution.
- Remove or exclude streaming/scraping, presence, canvas, telemetry/crash reporting, and OTA features; document each removal.
- Support local files, scanning, folders, M3U import/export, local lyrics, persistent queue/position, and Home/Search/Library/Settings navigation.
- Keep relevant tests, add tests for new code, and make a compiling commit for each stage.

## Decisions
- Use `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream` as the working clone of upstream rather than creating a fresh repository.
- Invoke Gradle as `bash ./gradlew ...` because the wrapper is not executable.
- Generated the standard debug keystore at `~/.android/debug.keystore` for the upstream baseline build.

## Work State
### Completed
- Cloned upstream; confirmed `origin` is `https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music.git` and the initial commit is `b10bf919 ci: remove nightly telegram workflow`.
- Confirmed upstream baseline build succeeds: `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug --no-configuration-cache --console=plain` (`757 actionable tasks: 120 executed, 637 up-to-date`).
- Inspected project modules, app configuration, Hilt DI, Room database, Media3 playback service, navigation, theme, manifest, and M3U/persistence code.
- Confirmed the upstream app has Room catalog, persisted queue/player state, and M3U metadata handling, but no local-device scanner or local-file playback path was found in the audited source.
- Confirmed Last.fm API credentials are hard-coded in `app/build.gradle.kts`; updater and online integration routes/modules are present.
- No source, documentation, tests, or commits have been created; `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream` is clean.

### Active
- Finish and write the architecture audit and requirement-by-requirement gap analysis.
- Plan and begin compiling AURA rebrand, scope removals, local library/playback, UI, tests, and documentation stages.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Write the audit and requirement-level Exists/Partial/Missing table, including module map, DI, database, playback, theme, SDK, and navigation findings.
2. Start the staged AURA changes, building and committing each compiling stage.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/settings.gradle.kts`: module declarations and project name.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts`: SDK levels, dependencies, flavors, and hard-coded Last.fm credentials.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`: permissions and app components.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/di/AppModule.kt`: dependency injection and cache provisions.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/MusicDatabase.kt`: Room entities, schema, and migrations.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/DatabaseDao.kt`: database queries.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt`: Media3 playback and persisted player state.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MediaLibrarySessionCallback.kt`: media catalog and browsing.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/extensions/MediaItemExt.kt`: media item construction.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/theme/Theme.kt`: theme and dynamic-color behavior.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt`: Compose routes, including online integrations.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/viewmodels/BackupRestoreViewModel.kt`: backup and M3U import handling.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/utils/PlaylistExporter.kt`: playlist export.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/README.md`: upstream branding, claims, and attribution.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/development_guide.md`: upstream setup/build guidance.

## Important Context
- Upstream modules include `:app`, `:innertube`, `:kizzy`, `:lastfm`, `:shazamkit`, `:artistvideo`, `:Motionartwork`, `:jiosaavn`, `:spotify`, and `:lyricsProvider`.
- App configuration: namespace `com.music.vivi`, applicationId `com.vivi.vivimusic`, minSdk 26, compileSdk/targetSdk 37, Java/Kotlin 21.
- M3U import/export currently handles playlist metadata rather than resolving local paths into playable tracks; local `.lrc` sidecar loading was not found.
- Discord presence, Last.fm, Canvas/artwork integrations, and an updater are present; targeted telemetry searches found no Firebase Analytics, Crashlytics, Sentry, Amplitude, or PostHog symbols.
