# AURA Music: upstream architecture and gap audit

Audit basis: upstream `vivizzz007/vivi-music` at `b10bf919` (`ci: remove nightly telegram workflow`), reviewed 2026-11-03. The repository is GPL-3.0. This document distinguishes the code that exists at that revision from the requested AURA Music local-only product scope.

## Build and project configuration

- Root Gradle project name: `vivimusic`; Android application module: `:app`.
- The app uses Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Hilt, Room/KSP, DataStore, Media3, and Protocol Buffers.
- Android namespace: `com.music.vivi`; application ID: `com.vivi.vivimusic`.
- `minSdk = 26`, `compileSdk = 37`, `targetSdk = 37`; Java and Kotlin JVM target 21.
- Build flavors include `foss`/`gms` and universal/ABI variants. The `foss` flavor disables Cast availability; the GMS flavor enables it.
- `app/build.gradle.kts` contains embedded Last.fm API key and secret values. These are upstream credentials and must not be copied into an offline AURA build.
- The upstream baseline was verified with `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug --no-configuration-cache --console=plain` (757 actionable tasks; 120 executed, 637 up-to-date). The wrapper file is not executable in this checkout, hence the explicit `bash` invocation.

## Module map

| Module | Upstream role | AURA disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `:app` | Android UI, app lifecycle, dependency injection, Room, Media3 service, widgets and integrations | Retain and rework for AURA local playback |
| `:innertube` | YouTube Music/Innertube networking and extraction | Remove from AURA runtime/build |
| `:jiosaavn` | JioSaavn search/streaming integration | Remove from AURA runtime/build |
| `:spotify` | Spotify API/Canvas integration | Remove from AURA runtime/build |
| `:lastfm` | Last.fm integration/scrobbling | Remove from AURA runtime/build |
| `:kizzy` | Discord rich-presence integration | Remove from AURA runtime/build |
| `:shazamkit` | ShazamKit integration | Remove from AURA runtime/build |
| `:artistvideo` | Artist-video feature | Remove from AURA runtime/build |
| `:Motionartwork` | Motion artwork/Canvas provider | Remove from AURA runtime/build |
| `:lyricsProvider` | Online lyrics providers/scraping | Remove from AURA runtime/build; retain only sidecar/local lyrics support if needed |

The exact dependency edges and unused code should be rechecked as each module is detached; deleting source modules before Gradle references and UI entry points are removed risks breaking compilation.

## Architecture findings

### Dependency injection

The app is Hilt-based. `app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/di/AppModule.kt` supplies application-level dependencies, including cache-related objects. Feature and persistence services are injected into ViewModels and the playback service. AURA should keep Hilt and bind local catalog/scanner and local-file access abstractions rather than online providers.

### Database and persistence

`app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/MusicDatabase.kt` and `DatabaseDao.kt` define the Room database and queries. Upstream already has catalog-oriented song/album/artist/playlist data and database migrations. Playback queue/player state is persisted through the existing preference/state layer. The upstream database is designed primarily around remote catalog IDs and metadata; local URI, stable file identity, folder membership, and scan state are not established as a complete local-library model. Prefer additive schema changes with migrations, not destructive recreation.

M3U import/export exists in `BackupRestoreViewModel.kt` and `utils/PlaylistExporter.kt`, but it is oriented around playlist/catalog metadata and does not provide complete robust resolution of local filesystem entries into playable tracks. AURA needs path/URI-aware import/export and missing-file handling.

### Playback

`playback/MusicService.kt` uses Media3 and persists playback state; `MediaLibrarySessionCallback.kt` exposes a media library/session. Existing media item construction (`extensions/MediaItemExt.kt`) assumes upstream media identities and can participate in remote stream resolution. AURA must ensure that queue items use local content URIs and that the service resolves only locally authorized media, with notification/background playback and restart restoration retained.

No local-device media scanner or end-to-end local-file playback path was found in the audited app source. Local permission handling, MediaStore indexing, folder browsing and selection, and `.lrc` sidecar discovery are gaps.

### UI, navigation, and theme

The interface is a large Jetpack Compose application with player, library, search, settings, playlist, online integration, and updater routes. `ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt` includes online integrations. The theme is defined in `ui/theme/Theme.kt`, including Material You/dynamic color behavior. AURA requires its own monochrome palette/assets and a pared-down primary navigation for Home, Search, Library and Settings. Search should only search the indexed local catalog.

Canvas is overloaded in upstream source to refer both to the online animated artwork feature and to Compose drawing primitives. Removing animated online Canvas artwork must not remove Compose `Canvas` uses for sliders, lyric rendering, or other local UI drawing.

## Requirement-by-requirement gap analysis

| Requirement | Status at upstream revision | Evidence / work required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GPL-3.0 derivative with upstream history and remote preserved | Exists as foundation | Repository has upstream history and `origin`; retain LICENSE and relevant copyright notices, document AURA modifications and attribution. |
| AURA Music name, monochrome identity and assets | Missing | Project/app branding remains Vivi Music; update app labels, icons, splash/metadata, theme and documentation without removing upstream notices. |
| Local-only operation; no network audio/metadata acquisition | Missing | Innertube, JioSaavn, Spotify and lyrics provider integrations are included. Remove dependencies/routes and ensure local player has no network fallback. |
| Local device audio scanning/indexing | Missing | No complete MediaStore scanner was found. Implement permission-aware scan, refresh and catalog persistence. |
| Folder browsing | Missing | Build a local folder view backed by indexed local URIs/paths. |
| Local file playback | Missing | Existing Media3 session/player is reusable, but local content URI construction/resolution is not a full app path. |
| M3U import/export for local tracks | Partial | Import/export utilities exist, but local paths, URI permissions, unavailable items and local queue mapping need implementation and tests. |
| Local `.lrc` lyrics | Missing | Existing lyrics are provider/online oriented; implement same-directory sidecar lookup and timed/plain text parsing. |
| Persistent queue and playback position | Partial / present | Existing database/preferences and service persist player state. Verify restart restoration specifically for local content URIs and update/add regression tests. |
| Home, Search, Library, Settings navigation | Partial | Equivalent navigation and settings exist among larger online-oriented surfaces; simplify and rewire search/library to local data only. |
| Remove Discord presence | Present upstream; remove | `:kizzy` and associated preferences/service/UI must not be included. |
| Remove animated Canvas/artwork online features | Present upstream; remove | `:Motionartwork`, Spotify Canvas, artwork fetching and related settings/routes; retain ordinary Compose drawing Canvas. |
| Remove analytics and crash telemetry | No targeted analytics/crash SDK found in inspected app source | No Firebase Analytics/Crashlytics, Sentry, Amplitude or PostHog symbols were found by the initial targeted search. Recheck all dependencies, manifest providers and build plugins before claiming removal. |
| Remove OTA/updater | Present upstream; remove | Updater workers, download/install flows, release checks, update routes/notifications and update-specific permissions should be removed. |
| Remove hard-coded online credentials | Present upstream; remove | Last.fm values in `app/build.gradle.kts` must be deleted along with the provider integration. |
| Tests for local behavior and retained behavior | Missing for new functionality | Keep applicable upstream tests; add scanner, M3U, lyrics, URI playback/persistence tests and run available test/build tasks per stage. |

## Removal and retention policy

Remove networking and online service integrations, not useful local Android infrastructure. Retain the Media3 playback service/session, Room and migrations, queue state, local playlist management, notification/background playback, widgets only if they work wholly from local data, and Compose drawing primitives. Explicitly document removed features and do not leave reachable UI routes or hidden background work for the removed services.

## Staged implementation and verification

Changes are intended to be split into small buildable commits: (1) audit/branding and app identity; (2) offline scope and online feature detachment; (3) local catalog/scanning and folder UI; (4) local playback and persistent queue; (5) local playlists and lyrics; (6) final navigation/theme/docs and full requirement review. Each stage should run its narrow tests and compile check before committing. The baseline build is not evidence that the AURA modifications compile.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build AURA Music as a GPL-3.0 local-only derivative of `vivizzz007/vivi-music`, preserving upstream history and remote.
- Audit upstream, then implement the player in compiling stages, with a final gap analysis, removal log, attribution, and build/test results.

## Requirements
- Document upstream modules, DI, database, playback service, theme, SDK levels, UI, and requirement-by-requirement gaps.
- Rebrand as AURA Music with monochrome styling/assets while retaining upstream copyright notices and GPL-3.0 attribution.
- Remove or exclude streaming/scraping, presence, online Canvas artwork, telemetry/crash reporting, and OTA features; document removals.
- Support local files, scanning, folders, M3U import/export, local lyrics, persistent queue/position, and Home/Search/Library/Settings navigation.
- Retain relevant tests, add tests for new code, and build and commit each stage.

## Decisions
- Use `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream` as the working clone; retain upstream history and `origin`.
- Invoke Gradle via `bash ./gradlew ...`.
- Use local Git author identity `AURA Agent <aura-agent@users.noreply.github.com>` after Git rejected the empty default identity.

## Work State
### Completed
- Cloned upstream and confirmed `origin` is `https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music.git`; initial commit is `b10bf919`.
- Verified upstream baseline build with `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug --no-configuration-cache --console=plain` (757 actionable tasks; 120 executed, 637 up-to-date).
- Inspected Gradle configuration, module map, DI, Room database, Media3 playback, navigation, theme, and manifest.
- Created `docs/AURA_UPSTREAM_AUDIT.md` with architecture findings and a requirement-by-requirement gap analysis.
- Committed the audit as `12fff80d docs(audit): document upstream architecture and AURA gaps`.

### Active
- Begin AURA branding and staged implementation; source inspection has started, but no app code or assets have been changed.
- Two background codebase audits are pending: playback/storage and online-feature inventory.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Collect the pending audit findings and complete the branding/removal inventory.
2. Implement branding and app identity changes, run the build, and commit that stage.
3. Proceed through online-feature detachment, local scanning/folders, playback/persistence, playlists/lyrics, and final navigation/theme; test and commit each stage.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/docs/AURA_UPSTREAM_AUDIT.md`: committed architecture audit and gap analysis.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts`: SDK, flavors, dependencies, and upstream Last.fm credentials.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`: permissions and app components/routes.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/theme/Theme.kt`: theme and dynamic-color implementation.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/res/values/app_name.xml`: current app label.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/res/values/styles.xml`: current theme resources.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/settings.gradle.kts`: included upstream modules.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt`: Media3 playback service.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/MusicDatabase.kt`: Room schema and migrations.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt`: Compose routes.

## Important Context
- Upstream has Room catalog, persisted queue/player state, Media3 playback, and M3U utilities, but no complete local-device scanner or local-file playback path was found.
- M3U handling is metadata-oriented; local path/URI resolution and `.lrc` sidecar loading are missing.
- Online integrations include `:innertube`, `:jiosaavn`, `:spotify`, `:lastfm`, `:kizzy`, `:shazamkit`, `:artistvideo`, `:Motionartwork`, and `:lyricsProvider`.
- `app/build.gradle.kts` embeds Last.fm credentials. Targeted searches found no Firebase Analytics/Crashlytics, Sentry, Amplitude, or PostHog symbols.
- Online animated Canvas artwork must be distinguished from Compose `Canvas` drawing used by local UI components.

1: # AURA Music: upstream architecture and gap audit
2: 
3: Audit basis: upstream `vivizzz007/vivi-music` at `b10bf919` (`ci: remove nightly telegram workflow`), reviewed 2026-11-03. The repository is GPL-3.0. This document distinguishes the code that exists at that revision from the requested AURA Music local-only product scope.
4: 
5: ## Build and project configuration
6: 
7: - Root Gradle project name: `vivimusic`; Android application module: `:app`.
8: - The app uses Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Hilt, Room/KSP, DataStore, Media3, and Protocol Buffers.
9: - Android namespace: `com.music.vivi`; application ID: `com.vivi.vivimusic`.
10: - `minSdk = 26`, `compileSdk = 37`, `targetSdk = 37`; Java and Kotlin JVM target 21.
11: - Build flavors include `foss`/`gms` and universal/ABI variants. The `foss` flavor disables Cast availability; the GMS flavor enables it.
12: - `app/build.gradle.kts` contains embedded Last.fm API key and secret values. These are upstream credentials and must not be copied into an offline AURA build.
13: - The upstream baseline was verified with `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug --no-configuration-cache --console=plain` (757 actionable tasks; 120 executed, 637 up-to-date). The wrapper file is not executable in this checkout, hence the explicit `bash` invocation.
14: 
15: ## Module map
16: 
17: | Module | Upstream role | AURA disposition |
18: | --- | --- | --- |
19: | `:app` | Android UI, app lifecycle, dependency injection, Room, Media3 service, widgets and integrations | Retain and rework for AURA local playback |
20: | `:innertube` | YouTube Music/Innertube networking and extraction | Remove from AURA runtime/build |
21: | `:jiosaavn` | JioSaavn search/streaming integration | Remove from AURA runtime/build |
22: | `:spotify` | Spotify API/Canvas integration | Remove from AURA runtime/build |
23: | `:lastfm` | Last.fm integration/scrobbling | Remove from AURA runtime/build |
24: | `:kizzy` | Discord rich-presence integration | Remove from AURA runtime/build |
25: | `:shazamkit` | ShazamKit integration | Remove from AURA runtime/build |
26: | `:artistvideo` | Artist-video feature | Remove from AURA runtime/build |
27: | `:Motionartwork` | Motion artwork/Canvas provider | Remove from AURA runtime/build |
28: | `:lyricsProvider` | Online lyrics providers/scraping | Remove from AURA runtime/build; retain only sidecar/local lyrics support if needed |
29: 
30: The exact dependency edges and unused code should be rechecked as each module is detached; deleting source modules before Gradle references and UI entry points are removed risks breaking compilation.
31: 
32: ## Architecture findings
33: 
34: ### Dependency injection
35: 
36: The app is Hilt-based. `app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/di/AppModule.kt` supplies application-level dependencies, including cache-related objects. Feature and persistence services are injected into ViewModels and the playback service. AURA should keep Hilt and bind local catalog/scanner and local-file access abstractions rather than online providers.
37: 
38: ### Database and persistence
39: 
40: `app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/MusicDatabase.kt` and `DatabaseDao.kt` define the Room database and queries. Upstream already has catalog-oriented song/album/artist/playlist data and database migrations. Playback queue/player state is persisted through the existing preference/state layer. The upstream database is designed primarily around remote catalog IDs and metadata; local URI, stable file identity, folder membership, and scan state are not established as a complete local-library model. Prefer additive schema changes with migrations, not destructive recreation.
41: 
42: M3U import/export exists in `BackupRestoreViewModel.kt` and `utils/PlaylistExporter.kt`, but it is oriented around playlist/catalog metadata and does not provide complete robust resolution of local filesystem entries into playable tracks. AURA needs path/URI-aware import/export and missing-file handling.
43: 
44: ### Playback
45: 
46: `playback/MusicService.kt` uses Media3 and persists playback state; `MediaLibrarySessionCallback.kt` exposes a media library/session. Existing media item construction (`extensions/MediaItemExt.kt`) assumes upstream media identities and can participate in remote stream resolution. AURA must ensure that queue items use local content URIs and that the service resolves only locally authorized media, with notification/background playback and restart restoration retained.
47: 
48: No local-device media scanner or end-to-end local-file playback path was found in the audited app source. Local permission handling, MediaStore indexing, folder browsing and selection, and `.lrc` sidecar discovery are gaps.
49: 
50: ### UI, navigation, and theme
51: 
52: The interface is a large Jetpack Compose application with player, library, search, settings, playlist, online integration, and updater routes. `ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt` includes online integrations. The theme is defined in `ui/theme/Theme.kt`, including Material You/dynamic color behavior. AURA requires its own monochrome palette/assets and a pared-down primary navigation for Home, Search, Library and Settings. Search should only search the indexed local catalog.
53: 
54: Canvas is overloaded in upstream source to refer both to the online animated artwork feature and to Compose drawing primitives. Removing animated online Canvas artwork must not remove Compose `Canvas` uses for sliders, lyric rendering, or other local UI drawing.
55: 
56: ## Requirement-by-requirement gap analysis
57: 
58: | Requirement | Status at upstream revision | Evidence / work required |
59: | --- | --- | --- |
60: | GPL-3.0 derivative with upstream history and remote preserved | Exists as foundation | Repository has upstream history and `origin`; retain LICENSE and relevant copyright notices, document AURA modifications and attribution. |
61: | AURA Music name, monochrome identity and assets | Missing | Project/app branding remains Vivi Music; update app labels, icons, splash/metadata, theme and documentation without removing upstream notices. |
62: | Local-only operation; no network audio/metadata acquisition | Missing | Innertube, JioSaavn, Spotify and lyrics provider integrations are included. Remove dependencies/routes and ensure local player has no network fallback. |
63: | Local device audio scanning/indexing | Missing | No complete MediaStore scanner was found. Implement permission-aware scan, refresh and catalog persistence. |
64: | Folder browsing | Missing | Build a local folder view backed by indexed local URIs/paths. |
65: | Local file playback | Missing | Existing Media3 session/player is reusable, but local content URI construction/resolution is not a full app path. |
66: | M3U import/export for local tracks | Partial | Import/export utilities exist, but local paths, URI permissions, unavailable items and local queue mapping need implementation and tests. |
67: | Local `.lrc` lyrics | Missing | Existing lyrics are provider/online oriented; implement same-directory sidecar lookup and timed/plain text parsing. |
68: | Persistent queue and playback position | Partial / present | Existing database/preferences and service persist player state. Verify restart restoration specifically for local content URIs and update/add regression tests. |
69: | Home, Search, Library, Settings navigation | Partial | Equivalent navigation and settings exist among larger online-oriented surfaces; simplify and rewire search/library to local data only. |
70: | Remove Discord presence | Present upstream; remove | `:kizzy` and associated preferences/service/UI must not be included. |
71: | Remove animated Canvas/artwork online features | Present upstream; remove | `:Motionartwork`, Spotify Canvas, artwork fetching and related settings/routes; retain ordinary Compose drawing Canvas. |
72: | Remove analytics and crash telemetry | No targeted analytics/crash SDK found in inspected app source | No Firebase Analytics/Crashlytics, Sentry, Amplitude or PostHog symbols were found by the initial targeted search. Recheck all dependencies, manifest providers and build plugins before claiming removal. |
73: | Remove OTA/updater | Present upstream; remove | Updater workers, download/install flows, release checks, update routes/notifications and update-specific permissions should be removed. |
74: | Remove hard-coded online credentials | Present upstream; remove | Last.fm values in `app/build.gradle.kts` must be deleted along with the provider integration. |
75: | Tests for local behavior and retained behavior | Missing for new functionality | Keep applicable upstream tests; add scanner, M3U, lyrics, URI playback/persistence tests and run available test/build tasks per stage. |
76: 
77: ## Removal and retention policy
78: 
79: Remove networking and online service integrations, not useful local Android infrastructure. Retain the Media3 playback service/session, Room and migrations, queue state, local playlist management, notification/background playback, widgets only if they work wholly from local data, and Compose drawing primitives. Explicitly document removed features and do not leave reachable UI routes or hidden background work for the removed services.
80: 
81: ## Staged implementation and verification
82: 
83: Changes are intended to be split into small buildable commits: (1) audit/branding and app identity; (2) offline scope and online feature detachment; (3) local catalog/scanning and folder UI; (4) local playback and persistent queue; (5) local playlists and lyrics; (6) final navigation/theme/docs and full requirement review. Each stage should run its narrow tests and compile check before committing. The baseline build is not evidence that the AURA modifications compile.

## Findings

- **Room database and DAO — present.** The app has a Room schema for songs, artists, albums, playlists, lyrics, and related data, with broad query and upsert support. `SongEntity` includes an `isLocal` flag, but that flag alone doesn’t establish device-file scanning or playback.  
  [MusicDatabase.kt](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/MusicDatabase.kt#L91) · [DatabaseDao.kt](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/DatabaseDao.kt#L647) · [SongEntity.kt](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/entities/SongEntity.kt#L28) · [LyricsEntity.kt](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/entities/LyricsEntity.kt#L12)

- **Queue and player-state persistence — present.** `MusicService` saves and restores queue, automix queue, and player state in `filesDir`; the persisted data includes queue type, current item/index and position, and player settings such as volume.  
  [MusicService.kt](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt#L1133) · [PersistQueue.kt](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/models/PersistQueue.kt#L10) · [PersistPlayerState.kt](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/models/PersistPlayerState.kt#L10)

- **Media3 playback service — present.** Playback is managed by `MusicService`, and the service sets Media3 media items and queues.  
  [MusicService.kt](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt#L252)

- **Device-local audio scanning and file playback — not found.** The searched Kotlin sources had no `MediaStore.Audio` scanning implementation. The `isLocal` database marker and local-named queue classes don’t by themselves demonstrate scanning device audio or playing file URIs; that functionality remains unverified.

- **M3U — export and limited import exist.** Export writes `#EXTINF` metadata and YouTube URLs. Import reads `#EXTINF` artist/title text into placeholder songs with empty IDs; it does not resolve the playlist’s path/URL entries to existing songs or files.

## Audit findings

The upstream app has multiple online surfaces, so removing `:innertube` by itself would not make it local-only. The app’s startup, UI, ViewModels, playback, lyrics, and background work all have integration call sites. Detach those call sites before removing their modules or the build will break.

- **Streaming, scraping, and online catalog:** `:innertube` is used across the app, including by search and browse ViewModels, menus, playback queues, and release checks. Startup also initializes YouTube state and the stream extractor. App-local lyrics providers include YouTube and Spotify, so removing `:lyricsProvider` alone does not remove all online lyrics. Solver assets are also present.
- **Other online integrations:** The app depends on `:jiosaavn`, `:spotify`, `:lastfm`, `:kizzy`, `:shazamkit`, `:artistvideo`, `:Motionartwork`, and `:lyricsProvider`. App code also has Listen Together and other online-facing routes; assess those separately if the requirement is *no network access*, not just removal of music providers.
- **Presence:** Discord RPC is connected to playback and has settings/login UI. Detach those hooks and screens as well as `:kizzy`.
- **Canvas/artwork:** Motion artwork and Spotify Canvas are fetched from online providers and integrated into player rendering and caching. Keep ordinary Compose and Android drawing `Canvas` uses; they are UI primitives, not the online artwork feature.
- **Background work:** `NewReleaseCheckWorker` makes periodic YouTube artist/release checks and is scheduled from `App`. WorkManager is also used for auto-backup, so removing updater workers is not a reason to remove WorkManager wholesale.
- **Crash handling and telemetry:** The custom `CrashHandler` and `CrashActivity` locally create and display a crash log; the inspected code does not show them uploading it. Targeted searches found no Firebase Analytics/Crashlytics, Sentry, Amplitude, or PostHog symbols. Media3 `AnalyticsListener`/`PlaybackStats` are playback instrumentation, not evidence of a third-party telemetry SDK. Before claiming telemetry is absent, also check the resolved dependency graph and merged manifest.
- **OTA updating:** Updates are reachable through startup checks, settings and navigation, download workers, notifications, and install/download flows. Remove the whole feature path, not only the updater package.
- **Credentials:** `app/build.gradle.kts` contains hard-coded Last.fm API key and secret values. Remove them with the integration; do not carry them into an AURA build.
- **Shared infrastructure to protect:** Keep Media3 playback/session, Room and migrations, queue state, local playlist management, notification/background playback, and Compose drawing. Recheck each service before removing it: some similarly named download or worker infrastructure may have separate local-app uses.

## Safe removal/exclusion plan

1. **Detach features first.** Remove online routes, settings, ViewModel/service hooks, startup initialization, scheduled work, and notifications. In particular, trace YouTube usage through the app before changing `:innertube`; retain or replace the local functionality that currently depends on shared models or queue types.
2. **Remove project dependencies second.** Once app call sites are detached, remove the relevant `implementation(project(...))` entries from the app build file and the matching `include(...)` entries from `settings.gradle.kts`. Remove credentials and feature-only DI/cache providers alongside their consumers.
3. **Remove only online artwork code.** Delete provider fetch/render/cache paths and their settings, but retain Compose/Android canvas drawing used for controls, charts, widgets, or other local UI.
4. **Remove updater paths as a unit.** Include release checks, update settings/routes, download/install workers and UI, update notifications, and updater-only state. Keep WorkManager while auto-backup still uses it.
5. **Review the manifest after detaching features.** Remove YouTube/online app-link filters and permissions only when their features are gone. Keep playback service and media-button components. Reassess network, microphone, and storage permissions against remaining uses; verify the **merged** manifest rather than relying only on the source manifest.
6. **Verify the offline boundary.** Search app code and dependencies for remaining network clients, provider calls, remote image/audio fallbacks, and scheduled online work. Then build and test local playback, queue restoration, playlists, notifications, and backup without the online modules.

## Objective
- Build AURA Music as a GPL-3.0 local-only derivative of `vivizzz007/vivi-music`, preserving upstream history and remote.
- Audit upstream, implement the app in buildable stages, and finish with a gap analysis, removal log, attribution, and test/build results.

## Requirements
- Document upstream architecture, DI, database, playback service, theme, SDK levels, UI, and requirement-by-requirement gaps.
- Rebrand as AURA Music with monochrome styling/assets while retaining upstream copyright notices and GPL-3.0 attribution.
- Remove or exclude streaming/scraping, presence, online Canvas artwork, telemetry/crash reporting, and OTA features; document removals.
- Support local files, scanning, folders, M3U import/export, local lyrics, persistent queue/position, and Home/Search/Library/Settings navigation.
- Retain relevant tests, add tests for new code, and build and commit each stage.

## Decisions
- Use `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream` as the working clone; retain upstream history and `origin` (`https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music.git`).
- Invoke Gradle via `bash ./gradlew ...`.
- Use local Git author identity `AURA Agent <aura-agent@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Verified upstream baseline build and committed the architecture/gap audit as `12fff80d docs(audit): document upstream architecture and AURA gaps`.
- Implemented initial, uncommitted branding edits: AURA Music label and application ID, project name, monochrome launcher foreground, black default theme seed, and AURA theme/style names.
- Completed playback/storage and online-feature inventories; confirmed no device-local audio scanner/playback path was found upstream.

### Active
- Fix branding-stage compile errors, verify build, and commit the stage.
- Continue staged removal of online features, then implement local scanning/folders, playback/persistence, playlists/lyrics, navigation/theme, tests, and final gap/removal documentation.

### Blocked
- Current build fails because some old `vivimusicTheme` references/imports remain while call sites were renamed to `auraMusicTheme`; errors are in `MainActivity.kt`, `WelcomeActivity.kt`, `CrashActivity.kt`, and `ThemeSettings.kt`.

## Next Move
1. Search for all `vivimusicTheme` imports/usages, update remaining references consistently, and rerun `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug --no-configuration-cache --console=plain`.
2. Run `git diff --check`, review the branding diff, update the implementation log with build results, and commit the branding stage.
3. Detach online features and their app call sites before removing module dependencies; preserve local playback, Room, WorkManager backup, notifications, and Compose drawing.
4. Implement and verify the remaining local-only capabilities in the planned stages, committing each buildable stage.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/docs/AURA_UPSTREAM_AUDIT.md`: committed upstream architecture and requirement-gap audit.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/docs/AURA_IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md`: staged implementation/removal log; currently records initial branding.

- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/WelcomeActivity.kt`: remaining old theme references causing compile failure.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/CrashActivity.kt`: theme imports/call sites; current compile failure.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/settings/ThemeSettings.kt`: theme imports/call sites; current compile failure.

- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/settings.gradle.kts`: project name and included online modules.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`: permissions, components, and online intent filters.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/App.kt`: startup integrations and release-check scheduling.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt`: Media3 playback and integration hooks.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt`: online/update routes and navigation.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/vivimusic/release/NewReleaseCheckWorker.kt`: online release-check worker.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/utils/AutoBackupHelper.kt`: local backup functionality to preserve.

## Important Context
- Branding changes are uncommitted; the last `assembleDebug` failed at Kotlin compilation due to unresolved `vivimusicTheme`/`auraMusicTheme` references.
- The upstream branch is `main`, one commit ahead of `origin/main` due to the audit commit.
- Online integrations include `:innertube`, `:jiosaavn`, `:spotify`, `:lastfm`, `:kizzy`, `:shazamkit`, `:artistvideo`, `:Motionartwork`, and `:lyricsProvider`; detach app call sites before removing modules.
- Upstream already has Room catalog, persisted queue/player state, Media3 playback, M3U utilities, and lyrics storage, but no complete local-device scanner/file playback path; M3U import does not resolve entries to local files.
- `MusicService` persistence and local auto-backup should be retained; WorkManager also handles local backup.
- No third-party analytics/crash SDK symbols were found in targeted searches; upstream crash handling appears local, so verify resolved dependencies and merged manifest before documenting telemetry absence/removal.

## Objective
- Build AURA Music as a GPL-3.0 local-only derivative of `vivizzz007/vivi-music`, preserving upstream history and remote.
- Audit upstream, implement and verify the app in buildable stages, then document gaps, removals, attribution, and test/build results.

## Requirements
- Document upstream architecture, DI, database, playback service, theme, SDK levels, UI, and requirement-by-requirement gaps.
- Rebrand as AURA Music with monochrome styling/assets while retaining upstream copyright notices and GPL-3.0 attribution.
- Remove or exclude streaming/scraping, presence, online Canvas artwork, telemetry/crash reporting, and OTA features; document removals.
- Support local files, scanning, folders, M3U import/export, local lyrics, persistent queue/position, and Home/Search/Library/Settings navigation.
- Retain relevant tests, add tests for new code, and build and commit each stage.

## Decisions
- Use `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream` as the working clone; retain upstream history and `origin` (`https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music.git`).
- Invoke Gradle via `bash ./gradlew ...`.
- Use local Git author identity `AURA Agent <aura-agent@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Verified upstream baseline build and committed the architecture/gap audit as `12fff80d docs(audit): document upstream architecture and AURA gaps`.
- Implemented AURA identity and monochrome branding; fixed stale `vivimusicTheme` references.
- `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug --no-configuration-cache --console=plain` succeeded; `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Record the branding-stage build result in the implementation log and commit the uncommitted branding changes.
- Continue staged removal of online features, then implement local scanning/folders, playback/persistence, playlists/lyrics, navigation/theme, tests, and final gap/removal documentation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Update `docs/AURA_IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md` with the successful branding build, review the current diff, and commit the branding stage.
2. Detach online features and app call sites before removing module dependencies; preserve local playback, Room, WorkManager backup, notifications, and Compose drawing.
3. Implement and verify the remaining local-only capabilities in buildable stages, committing each one.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/docs/AURA_UPSTREAM_AUDIT.md`: committed upstream architecture and requirement-gap audit.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/docs/AURA_IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md`: stage/removal log; branding stage needs build result and commit record.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/theme/Theme.kt`: AURA theme and monochrome default.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts`: application ID and online dependencies/embedded Last.fm credentials.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/settings.gradle.kts`: project name and included online modules.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`: permissions, components, and online intent filters.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/App.kt`: startup integrations and release-check scheduling.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt`: Media3 playback and integration hooks.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt`: online/update routes and navigation.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/vivimusic/release/NewReleaseCheckWorker.kt`: online release-check worker.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/utils/AutoBackupHelper.kt`: local backup functionality to preserve.

## Important Context
- Branding changes are still uncommitted; audit commit `12fff80d` is committed. Build passed across debug variants with existing deprecation warnings and benign FOSS manifest-removal warnings.
- Online integrations include `:innertube`, `:jiosaavn`, `:spotify`, `:lastfm`, `:kizzy`, `:shazamkit`, `:artistvideo`, `:Motionartwork`, and `:lyricsProvider`; detach app call sites before removing modules.
- Upstream has Room catalog, persisted queue/player state, Media3 playback, M3U utilities, and lyrics storage, but no complete device-local audio scanner/file playback path; M3U import does not resolve entries to local files.
- `MusicService` persistence and local auto-backup should be retained; WorkManager also handles local backup.
- No third-party analytics/crash SDK symbols were found in targeted searches; upstream crash handling appears local. Verify resolved dependencies and merged manifest before documenting telemetry absence/removal.

197:             }

199:             return Result.success()
200:         } catch (e: Exception) {
201:             Timber.tag(TAG).e(e, "Error occurred during release check work")
202:             return Result.retry()
203:         } finally {
204:             database.close()
205:         }
206:     }
207: 
208:     companion object {
209:         private const val TAG = "NewReleaseCheckWorker"
210:         const val UNIQUE_WORK_NAME = "NewReleaseCheckWork"
211: 
212:         fun schedule(context: Context) {
213:             Timber.tag(TAG).d("Enqueuing periodic release check worker")
214:             val constraints = Constraints.Builder()
215:                 .setRequiredNetworkType(NetworkType.CONNECTED)
216:                 .build()
217: 
218:             val workRequest = PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder<NewReleaseCheckWorker>(
219:                 15, TimeUnit.MINUTES
220:             )
221:                 .setConstraints(constraints)
222:                 .addTag(UNIQUE_WORK_NAME)
223:                 .build()
224: 
225:             // UPDATE replaces any previously-stuck/misconfigured periodic work and resets the timer.
226:             WorkManager.getInstance(context).enqueueUniquePeriodicWork(
227:                 UNIQUE_WORK_NAME,
228:                 ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE,
229:                 workRequest
230:             )
231:         }
232: 
233:         fun cancel(context: Context) {
234:             Timber.tag(TAG).d("Cancelling periodic release check worker")
235:             WorkManager.getInstance(context).cancelUniqueWork(UNIQUE_WORK_NAME)
236:         }
237: 
238:         /**
239:          * Clears the seen-releases baseline and tracking timestamps so the worker treats
240:          * everything as unseen and re-snapshots on next run. Useful after a fresh install
241:          * or for testing.
242:          */
243:         fun clearSeenReleases(context: Context) {
244:             context.getSharedPreferences("new_release_prefs", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
245:                 .edit().clear().apply()
246:             Timber.tag(TAG).d("Cleared all seen release data — will re-snapshot on next run")
247:         }
248:     }
249: }

## Objective
- Build AURA Music as a GPL-3.0 local-only derivative of `vivizzz007/vivi-music`, preserving upstream history and remote.
- Audit upstream, implement and verify the app in buildable stages, then document gaps, removals, attribution, and test/build results.

## Requirements
- Document upstream architecture, DI, database, playback service, theme, SDK levels, UI, and requirement-by-requirement gaps.
- Rebrand as AURA Music with monochrome styling/assets while retaining upstream copyright notices and GPL-3.0 attribution.
- Remove or exclude streaming/scraping, presence, online Canvas artwork, telemetry/crash reporting, and OTA features; document removals.
- Support local files, scanning, folders, M3U import/export, local lyrics, persistent queue/position, and Home/Search/Library/Settings navigation.
- Retain relevant tests, add tests for new code, and build and commit each stage.

## Decisions
- Use `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream` as the working clone; retain upstream history and `origin` (`https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music.git`).
- Invoke Gradle via `bash ./gradlew ...`.
- Use local Git author identity `AURA Agent <aura-agent@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Verified upstream baseline build and committed architecture/gap audit as `12fff80d docs(audit): document upstream architecture and AURA gaps`.
- Implemented AURA identity and monochrome branding; fixed stale `vivimusicTheme` references.
- Branding build passed with `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug --no-configuration-cache --console=plain`; `git diff --check` passed.
- Committed branding changes as `2eac54c8 chore(branding): rebrand app as AURA Music`.

### Active
- Detach online features and app call sites before removing module dependencies; preserve local playback, Room, WorkManager backup, notifications, and Compose drawing.
- Continue implementing local scanning/folders, playback/persistence, playlists/lyrics, navigation/theme, tests, and final gap/removal documentation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Update `docs/AURA_IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md` to replace the branding stage’s `Commit: pending.` with `2eac54c8`.
2. Detach online routes, startup work, settings, and service hooks, then remove unused integrations/dependencies in buildable stages.
3. Build and test each stage, commit it, and proceed with local media capabilities.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/docs/AURA_UPSTREAM_AUDIT.md`: committed upstream architecture and requirement-gap audit.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/docs/AURA_IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md`: stage/removal log; branding commit entry needs updating.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/App.kt`: startup integrations and release-check scheduling.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/MainActivity.kt`: update checks and account/online UI call sites.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt`: Media3 playback and integration hooks.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt`: online/update routes and navigation.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/settings/UpdateSettings.kt`: updater settings UI.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/vivimusic/release/NewReleaseCheckWorker.kt`: online release-check worker.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts`: application ID and online dependencies/embedded Last.fm credentials.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/settings.gradle.kts`: project name and included online modules.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`: permissions, components, and online intent filters.

## Important Context
- Online integrations include `:innertube`, `:jiosaavn`, `:spotify`, `:lastfm`, `:kizzy`, `:shazamkit`, `:artistvideo`, `:Motionartwork`, and `:lyricsProvider`; detach app call sites before removing modules.
- Upstream has Room catalog, persisted queue/player state, Media3 playback, M3U utilities, and lyrics storage, but no complete device-local audio scanner/file playback path; M3U import does not resolve entries to local files.
- Preserve `MusicService` persistence and local auto-backup; WorkManager also handles local backup. Retain `FileProvider` while other share/export features depend on it.
- Initial audit found no external analytics/crash-reporting SDK; it did find local crash capture and playback-statistics code. Verify resolved dependencies, merged manifest, and online history-submission call sites before documenting telemetry absence/removal.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build AURA Music as a GPL-3.0 local-only derivative of `vivizzz007/vivi-music`, retaining upstream history and remote.
- Audit upstream, implement and verify the app in buildable stages, then document gaps, removals, attribution, and test/build results.

## Requirements
- Document upstream architecture, DI, database, playback service, theme, SDK levels, UI, and requirement-by-requirement gaps.
- Rebrand as AURA Music with monochrome styling/assets while retaining upstream copyright notices and GPL-3.0 attribution.
- Remove or exclude streaming/scraping, presence, online Canvas artwork, telemetry/crash reporting, and OTA features; document removals.
- Support local files, scanning, folders, M3U import/export, local lyrics, persistent queue/position, and Home/Search/Library/Settings navigation.
- Retain relevant tests, add tests for new code, and build and commit each stage.

## Decisions
- Use `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream` as the working clone; retain upstream history and `origin` (`https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music.git`).
- Invoke Gradle via `bash ./gradlew ...`.
- Use local Git author identity `AURA Agent <aura-agent@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Verified upstream baseline build and committed architecture/gap audit as `12fff80d docs(audit): document upstream architecture and AURA gaps`.
- Implemented AURA identity and monochrome branding; fixed stale `vivimusicTheme` references.
- Branding build passed with `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug --no-configuration-cache --console=plain`; `git diff --check` passed.
- Committed branding changes as `2eac54c8 chore(branding): rebrand app as AURA Music`.
- Updated `docs/AURA_IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md` branding entry to record commit `2eac54c8`; this documentation edit is uncommitted.

### Active
- Detach online routes, startup work, settings, and service hooks before removing integrations/dependencies; preserve local playback, Room, WorkManager backup, notifications, and Compose drawing.
- Continue implementing local scanning/folders, playback/persistence, playlists/lyrics, navigation/theme, tests, and final gap/removal documentation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Detach online routes and app call sites, beginning with startup integrations and update checks in `App.kt`, `MainActivity.kt`, and `NavigationBuilder.kt`.
2. Remove online settings links and service integration hooks, then remove unused modules/dependencies in buildable stages.
3. Build and test each stage, commit it, and proceed with local media capabilities.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/docs/AURA_IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md`: stage/removal log; branding commit entry is updated but uncommitted.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/docs/AURA_UPSTREAM_AUDIT.md`: committed upstream architecture and requirement-gap audit.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/App.kt`: startup integrations, online preferences, and release-check scheduling.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/MainActivity.kt`: online/update call sites and main navigation UI.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt`: online/update routes and navigation.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/settings/SettingsScreen.kt`: update and online settings links.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt`: Media3 playback plus Last.fm, Discord, and streaming hooks.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts`: online module dependencies and embedded Last.fm credentials.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/settings.gradle.kts`: project name and included online modules.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`: permissions, components, and online intent filters.

## Important Context
- Online integrations include `:innertube`, `:jiosaavn`, `:spotify`, `:lastfm`, `:kizzy`, `:shazamkit`, `:artistvideo`, `:Motionartwork`, and `:lyricsProvider`; detach app call sites before removing modules.
- `App.kt` initializes YouTube/KuGou/Last.fm, proxy and account state, and new-release checks; `MainActivity.kt` contains OTA checks, GitHub starring UI, and Listen Together hooks.
- `NavigationBuilder.kt` includes online search/browse/playlist, account, integration, updater, and recognition routes; `SettingsScreen.kt` links updater, account, Listen Together, and online-related settings.
- `MusicService.kt` is heavily coupled to YouTube queues/streaming, Last.fm scrobbling, Discord RPC, and Listen Together; preserve local playback, Room, and persistence when detaching.
- Upstream has Room catalog, persisted queue/player state, Media3 playback, M3U utilities, and lyrics storage, but no complete device-local audio scanner/file playback path; M3U import does not resolve entries to local files.
- Preserve `MusicService` persistence and local auto-backup. Verify resolved dependencies, merged manifest, and online history-submission call sites when documenting telemetry absence/removal.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e5ff9b1d2ffe3KMsKdgv6JdTP5" state="completed">
## Findings

**No files were edited.** The safest first step is to stop the automatic updater and background release-check triggers, while retaining the manual update UI, playback, database, and notification infrastructure.

### Automatic updater checks

- **App launch check:** `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/MainActivity.kt:419–457` runs a delayed `checkForUpdate(...)` when automatic checks are enabled. On success it saves the update-available state and may post an update notification. Its imports are at `:159–168`; some updater state is also read later at `:919–935`, so don’t remove those imports or listeners without checking their remaining uses.
- **Settings screen check:** `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/settings/SettingsScreen.kt:80–90` automatically checks when the main Settings screen opens. The update row and its `settings/update` navigation are at `:108–127`.
- **Updater settings check:** `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/settings/UpdateSettings.kt:139–151` also checks when that screen opens, if its auto-check preference is enabled.
- **Network implementation:** `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/vivimusic/updater/vivimusicupdater.kt:802–810` fetches GitHub releases. The update screen and its check behavior are in that file; `UpdateScreen` begins at `:126`, and its check is triggered around `:191–200`.

If the goal is **no automatic updater traffic**, disable the three screen-entry/startup checks above. Keep an explicitly user-triggered check in the updater screen if manual updating should remain available.

### Background new-release checks and notifications

- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/App.kt:280–304` clears a release-tracking baseline once and observes notification preferences to schedule or cancel `NewReleaseCheckWorker`.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/vivimusic/release/NewReleaseCheckWorker.kt:43–57, 102–110` reads local preferences/database state and fetches YouTube artist pages. Its scheduler requires network connectivity and enqueues periodic work at `:212–235`.

To stop that background traffic, remove or disable the `App` scheduling collector. If removing the whole release-check feature, also remove the one-time migration and its `NewReleaseCheckWorker` import at `App.kt:33, 280–287`. **Retain notification settings and other notification plumbing** unless those features are separately intended for removal.

### Other startup network activity—not updater checks

`/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/App.kt:159–209` contains startup observers that can perform network work:

- `:159–172` may request YouTube visitor data.
- `:174–209` may refresh an expired Spotify access token.

These are separate from release/update checking and may affect YouTube or Spotify functionality if removed.

One apparent GitHub check is **not a startup network request**: `MainActivity.kt:564–570` calls `GitHubViewModel.checkStarStatus`, which reads the saved `HasStarredRepoKey` preference in `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/github/GitHubViewModel.kt:53–57`. The view model has a separate service dependency, but that method does not call it.

### Navigation, compile dependencies, and playback to preserve

- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt:72–75, 340–350, 483–485` imports and registers updater-related screens/routes. These are **not required to remove automatic checks**; remove them only if removing the updater UI as a later step.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/settings/NotificationPermission.kt:105–129` includes general notification preferences and new-release notification preferences. Don’t treat this screen as updater-only.
- Preserve `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt:519–579`: it initializes the player and foreground/media notifications. Its Room-backed playback flows are at `:349–358`; these are unrelated to updater removal.

## Staged recommendation

1. **First, stop automatic network checks:** disable the `MainActivity` launch check, the `App` release-worker scheduling, and the settings-entry checks in `SettingsScreen` and `UpdateSettings`. This covers launch-time, background, and implicit settings-entry checks without deleting updater code.
2. **Keep the manual updater UI and routes** if users should still be able to check for and install updates on demand. Remove those routes and their dependencies only in a separate, broader updater-removal stage.
3. **Treat YouTube visitor-data and Spotify token refresh separately.** They are startup network activity, but removing them is a distinct product decision because they support those integrations.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e60018f94ffe1bo32sbgPNLX2q" state="completed" description="Audit online feature removal">
## Online-only integration inventory

The nine integration modules are included in the build and declared as app dependencies:

- `:innertube` — YouTube search, streaming, and library-related functionality
- `:jiosaavn`, `:spotify`, `:lastfm` — provider integrations and scrobbling
- `:kizzy`, `:shazamkit` — integrations to detach
- `:artistvideo`, `:Motionartwork` — online video/artwork features
- `:lyricsProvider` — lyrics providers

Their inclusion points are [`settings.gradle.kts`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/settings.gradle.kts) and [`app/build.gradle.kts`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts). Removing a module requires checking its app dependencies and source/UI references, not just removing it from the settings file.

Other online features found in the app include:

- YouTube deep-link routing, GitHub wiring, and updater checks in [`MainActivity.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/MainActivity.kt).
- Last.fm scrobbling and SponsorBlock alongside the playback service in [`MusicService.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt).
- Listen Together networking under [`app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/listentogether/`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/listentogether/).
- OTA download and installation under [`app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/vivimusic/updater/`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/vivimusic/updater/).
- Integration navigation, updater, changelog, and commits screens in [`NavigationBuilder.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt).
- Spotify Canvas and Motionartwork references in [`Player.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/player/Player.kt).
- Remote player-configuration updates in [`PlayerConfigStore.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/utils/cipher/PlayerConfigStore.kt).
- GitHub OAuth/API calls in [`GitHubService.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/github/network/GitHubService.kt).
- Apple Music album-description fetching in [`AppleMusicAboutAlbum.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/utils/AppleMusicAboutAlbum.kt), and Wikipedia summaries in [`Wikipedia.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/utils/Wikipedia.kt).
- Online lyrics, AI, and translation providers, in addition to the lyrics module.

## Manifest and configuration review

[`AndroidManifest.xml`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml) has `INTERNET` and `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE` permissions, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC`, YouTube/Listen Together/GitHub deep links, and a Listen Together receiver. Review each against the features retained: remove permissions, components, and intent filters only when no remaining app behavior needs them.

The Last.fm API key and secret are embedded in [`app/build.gradle.kts`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts); remove those values with the integration. Targeted searches found no Firebase Analytics/Crashlytics, Sentry, Amplitude, or PostHog SDK references.

## What to retain

Detaching online features should not remove local playback and app infrastructure: Media3 playback/session behavior, Room and migrations, queue state, local playlist management, notification/background playback, local content access, or unrelated Compose drawing. For example, [`BigSeekBar.kt`](/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/component/BigSeekBar.kt) uses `Canvas` for local UI drawing; that is separate from online animated artwork.

`ContentResolver` and `MediaStore` references support backups, exports, generated images, or resource access. The audit did not establish a complete local media-scanning/playback path, so preserve those call sites unless a more targeted review confirms they are unused.

## Shared dependencies

Ktor is used by integration modules and app-level online features; remove it only after those call sites are gone. Review OkHttp, Jsoup, and Media3’s OkHttp integration against remaining call sites before removing them. In particular, `:artistvideo` and Motionartwork have Media3 OkHttp call sites tied to online playback/artwork; those may disappear with the features, but should not be assumed redundant until checked.

## Audit corrections

The preliminary audit’s project identity claims were stale. The root project name is `aura-music`, the namespace is `com.music.vivi`, and the application ID is `com.aura.music`.

No files were edited.
</subagent>

## Objective
- Build AURA Music as a GPL-3.0 local-only derivative of `vivizzz007/vivi-music`, retaining upstream history and remote.
- Audit upstream, implement and verify the app in buildable stages, then document gaps, removals, attribution, and test/build results.

## Requirements
- Document upstream architecture, DI, database, playback service, theme, SDK levels, UI, and requirement-by-requirement gaps.
- Rebrand as AURA Music with monochrome styling/assets while retaining upstream copyright notices and GPL-3.0 attribution.
- Remove or exclude streaming/scraping, presence, online Canvas artwork, telemetry/crash reporting, and OTA features; document removals.
- Support local files, scanning, folders, M3U import/export, local lyrics, persistent queue/position, and Home/Search/Library/Settings navigation.
- Retain relevant tests, add tests for new code, and build and commit each stage.

## Decisions
- Use `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream` as the working clone; retain upstream history and `origin` (`https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music.git`).
- Use local Git author identity `AURA Agent <aura-agent@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Verified upstream baseline build and committed architecture/gap audit as `12fff80d docs(audit): document upstream architecture and AURA gaps`.
- Implemented AURA identity and monochrome branding; build passed and changes committed as `2eac54c8 chore(branding): rebrand app as AURA Music`.
- Removed automatic updater checks from app launch and settings entry, plus new-release worker scheduling from `App.kt`; manual updater UI/routes remain.
- `git diff --check` passed after the latest edits.

### Active
- Verify the automatic-check removal stage: `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug --no-configuration-cache --console=plain` exceeded its 120-second timeout before reporting completion.
- Continue detaching online routes, startup work, settings, and service hooks while preserving local playback, Room, WorkManager backup, notifications, and Compose drawing.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Rerun `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug --no-configuration-cache --console=plain` with a longer timeout and resolve any compile failures.
2. Update `docs/AURA_IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md` with the updater-check removal and verification, then commit the completed stage.
3. Detach online routes and app call sites, beginning with remaining startup integrations and update-related UI.
4. Remove online settings links and service integration hooks, then remove unused modules/dependencies in buildable stages.
5. Implement and test local media scanning/playback, folders, playlists, lyrics, and navigation; finish removal/gap documentation.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/docs/AURA_IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md`: stage/removal log; branding commit is documented, latest stage not yet recorded.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/docs/AURA_UPSTREAM_AUDIT.md`: committed upstream architecture and requirement-gap audit.

- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt`: Media3 playback plus Last.fm, Discord, streaming, and Listen Together hooks.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts` and `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/settings.gradle.kts`: online module dependencies and project configuration.
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`: permissions, components, and online intent filters.

## Important Context
- Latest edits are uncommitted across `App.kt`, `MainActivity.kt`, `SettingsScreen.kt`, `UpdateSettings.kt`, and `docs/AURA_IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md`; the build timed out before completion.
- Online modules include `:innertube`, `:jiosaavn`, `:spotify`, `:lastfm`, `:kizzy`, `:shazamkit`, `:artistvideo`, `:Motionartwork`, and `:lyricsProvider`; detach app call sites before removing them.

## Objective
- Build AURA Music as a GPL-3.0 local-only derivative of `vivizzz007/vivi-music`, retaining upstream history and remote.
- Audit upstream, implement and verify the app in buildable stages, and document gaps, removals, attribution, and test/build results.

## Requirements
- Document upstream architecture, DI, database, playback service, theme, SDK levels, UI, and requirement-by-requirement gaps.
- Rebrand as AURA Music with monochrome styling/assets while retaining upstream copyright notices and GPL-3.0 attribution.
- Remove or exclude streaming/scraping, presence, online Canvas artwork, telemetry/crash reporting, and OTA features; document removals.
- Support local files, scanning, folders, M3U import/export, local lyrics, persistent queue/position, and Home/Search/Library/Settings navigation.
- Retain relevant tests, add tests for new code, and build and commit each stage.

## Decisions
- Use `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream` as the working clone; retain upstream history and `origin` (`https://github.com/vivizzz007/vivi-music.git`).
- Use local Git author identity `AURA Agent <aura-agent@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Verified upstream baseline build and committed architecture/gap audit as `12fff80d docs(audit): document upstream architecture and AURA gaps`.
- Implemented AURA identity and monochrome branding; build passed and changes committed as `2eac54c8 chore(branding): rebrand app as AURA Music`.
- Removed automatic updater checks from app launch and settings entry, plus new-release worker scheduling from `App.kt`; `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug --no-configuration-cache --console=plain` succeeded.

### Active
- Record and commit the automatic-check removal stage; changes remain uncommitted across `App.kt`, `MainActivity.kt`, `SettingsScreen.kt`, `UpdateSettings.kt`, and `docs/AURA_IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md`.
- Detach online routes, startup work, settings, and service hooks while preserving local playback, Room, WorkManager backup, notifications, and Compose drawing.
- Implement and test local media scanning/playback, folders, playlists, lyrics, and navigation; finish removal/gap documentation.

### Blocked

<subagent sessionID="ses_e5ff2b6e2ffeSOaVFDIaEeAKS9" state="completed">
## Findings

The online features are not isolated behind Gradle modules: the app directly depends on nine feature modules, and several integrations are woven into playback, navigation, and persistence. Detach call sites and replace their responsibilities before removing module source or project references.

### Gradle boundary

`/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/settings.gradle.kts` includes `:app` and nine feature modules: `:innertube`, `:jiosaavn`, `:spotify`, `:lastfm`, `:kizzy`, `:shazamkit`, `:artistvideo`, `:Motionartwork`, and `:lyricsProvider`. The app declares direct dependencies on all nine in `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts` (lines 285–293), plus `libs.innertubex` (line 295). These are the clearest initial Gradle-removal candidates, after app call sites are rewired.

The app also declares Ktor directly—core, OkHttp, content negotiation, and JSON serialization—in `app/build.gradle.kts` (lines 301–304). **Do not remove those dependencies merely because the feature modules are detached.** App-owned Ktor consumers include remote stream extraction, online lyrics, GitHub operations, Wikipedia summaries, and Apple Music album descriptions:

- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/utils/InnerTubeXPlayer.kt`
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/lyrics/LrcRedLyricsProvider.kt`
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/github/network/GitHubService.kt`
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/utils/Wikipedia.kt`
- `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/utils/AppleMusicAboutAlbum.kt`

`/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/playlist/LocalPlaylistScreen.kt` also imports Ktor’s `ClientRequestException`; assess that reference when simplifying the playlist screen. After removing online consumers, recheck which Ktor artifacts remain necessary. The feature modules declare Ktor separately in their own Gradle files, so their dependencies disappear with those modules.

## Staged removal boundaries

1. **Detach navigation and online-only screens.**  
   Remove online integration routes and settings entry points in `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/ui/screens/NavigationBuilder.kt`. This includes Spotify, Motion artwork, SponsorBlock, Listen Together, and recognition routes. Also trace the screens and ViewModels they instantiate before dropping imports or dependencies.

2. **Separate online stream resolution from playback.**  
   `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/utils/YTPlayerUtils.kt` tries JioSaavn while resolving a YouTube stream. Removing that integration must not leave the YouTube resolver or remote fallback as the local-playback path; replace stream resolution with authorized local URIs.  
   `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/playback/MusicService.kt` mixes playback/session responsibilities with Last.fm, SponsorBlock, Spotify Canvas caching, and Listen Together. Remove those hooks selectively; retain the Media3 service, session, queue, and local playback responsibilities.

3. **Remove online integrations and app-owned networking.**  
   Spotify has playback/UI and Canvas connections; Last.fm has playback/scrobbling and settings hooks. Discord, artist video, animated artwork, and online lyrics also have app-facing surfaces. SponsorBlock and Listen Together are app-owned code rather than just feature-module dependencies, so removing project dependencies alone will not remove them.  
   Reassess the app-owned Ktor consumers above. GitHub/update functionality is online-facing; distinguish OTA/update work from local backup work rather than treating all WorkManager use as removable. `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/build.gradle.kts` also contains Last.fm credential build fields (lines 35–43), which belong with the Last.fm removal.

4. **Handle recognition persistence separately.**  
   ShazamKit removal spans recognition UI and app-owned recognition code, plus the Room entity and DAO. Recognition history is registered in `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/MusicDatabase.kt`, queried in `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/DatabaseDao.kt`, and defined in `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/db/entities/RecognitionHistory.kt`. It is present in database version 34 and `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/app/schemas/com.music.vivi.db.InternalDatabase/34.json`. Decide separately whether to retain or migrate the table; do not casually rely on destructive fallback behavior.

5. **Remove residual Gradle entries after source rewiring.**  
   Once routes, services, and providers no longer reference them, remove the nine `implementation(project(...))` entries from `app/build.gradle.kts` and the corresponding `include(...)` entries from `settings.gradle.kts`. Then remove `libs.innertubex` and any other libraries only after confirming they have no remaining consumers. Keep Gradle changes and source removal in buildable increments.

## Preserve

Keep Media3 playback and session infrastructure, Room and migrations, queue and playback-state persistence, local playlist management, notifications/background playback, and Compose drawing primitives. In particular, animated online “Canvas” artwork is separate from Compose `Canvas`, which is used for local UI drawing.

One important scope caveat: the audit found **no complete local-device scanner or end-to-end local-file playback path**. Retaining Media3 alone does not establish local-only playback; local URI construction/resolution, scanning, and catalog behavior still need to be verified or built. See `/tmp/opencode/aura-upstream/docs/AURA_UPSTREAM_AUDIT.md` for the broader architecture and local-only gap audit.

1: # AURA Music: upstream architecture and gap audit
2: 
3: Audit basis: upstream `vivizzz007/vivi-music` at `b10bf919` (`ci: remove nightly telegram workflow`), reviewed 2026-11-03. The repository is GPL-3.0. This document distinguishes the code that exists at that revision from the requested AURA Music local-only product scope.
4: 
5: ## Build and project configuration
6: 
7: - Root Gradle project name: `vivimusic`; Android application module: `:app`.
8: - The app uses Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Hilt, Room/KSP, DataStore, Media3, and Protocol Buffers.
9: - Android namespace: `com.music.vivi`; application ID: `com.vivi.vivimusic`.
10: - `minSdk = 26`, `compileSdk = 37`, `targetSdk = 37`; Java and Kotlin JVM target 21.
11: - Build flavors include `foss`/`gms` and universal/ABI variants. The `foss` flavor disables Cast availability; the GMS flavor enables it.
12: - `app/build.gradle.kts` contains embedded Last.fm API key and secret values. These are upstream credentials and must not be copied into an offline AURA build.
13: - The upstream baseline was verified with `bash ./gradlew assembleDebug --no-configuration-cache --console=plain` (757 actionable tasks; 120 executed, 637 up-to-date). The wrapper file is not executable in this checkout, hence the explicit `bash` invocation.
14:
